title: Organizational Change Management Partner
description:
The Business Information Services organization at Argonne is seeking an Organizational Change Management Partner to join their team. This position serves as a strategic change partner, helping leaders and initiative/project teams assess organizational impacts, prepare employees and managers, communicate effectively, manage resistance and risks, and achieve intended business outcomes. The position also advances Argonne’s OCM practice by developing and continuously improving methods, tools, templates, and best practices.

Responsibilities include:

  • Develops and implements organizational change-management strategies and plans for enterprise, directorate, department, program, process, technology, and workforce initiatives.
  • Advises leaders and initiative sponsors on the people, culture, process, technology, and organizational implications of proposed changes.
  • Determines the appropriate level of change-management support based on the magnitude, complexity, risk, interdependencies, and stakeholder impact of each initiative.
  • Integrates OCM activities, milestones, dependencies, risks, and resource requirements into project, program, product, and portfolio plans.
  • Applies a structured change-management methodology while tailoring approaches to the needs of Argonne’s environment.
  • Conducts organizational assessments, change-impact analyses, stakeholder analyses, role and job-impact assessments, readiness assessments, and change-risk assessments.
  • Develops comprehensive change-management plans, including stakeholder engagement, sponsorship, communications, training, coaching, resistance management, readiness, reinforcement, transition, and sustainment plans.
  • Acts as a trusted advisor and coach to executives, senior leaders, initiative sponsors, people managers, project managers, and other change agents.
  • Coaches sponsors and leaders on visible sponsorship, effective communication, decision-making, employee engagement, reinforcement, and accountability for change adoption.
  • Identifies, prepares, coaches, and supports Change Champions, super users, subject-matter experts, managers, and other local change agents.
  • Partners with communications and initiative teams to design, develop, deliver, and manage targeted change communications for different audiences and stages of the change journey.
  • Develops communication strategies, key messages, stakeholder-specific narratives, communication calendars, leadership talking points, frequently asked questions, feedback mechanisms, and other engagement materials.
  • Uses two-way communication and listening methods—including interviews, focus groups, surveys, workshops, office hours, and feedback channels—to identify concerns and improve the change approach.
  • Provides input into the design, development, delivery, and evaluation of training and performance-support programs required to enable successful adoption.
  • Partners with the learning organization to ensure that training and support materials are timely, accessible, role-specific, and aligned with the future state.
  • Tracks and reports change readiness, adoption, usage, proficiency, stakeholder engagement, training, communications effectiveness, risks, issues, and sustainment activities.
  • Uses qualitative and quantitative data to evaluate the effectiveness of OCM interventions and recommend adjustments.
  • Captures lessons learned, measures benefits realization in partnership with initiative leaders, and contributes to continuous improvement of the OCM practice.

Position Requirements

  • PA5: Bachelor's degree and 10+ years of related experience, or a Masters degree and 6+ years of experience, or equivalent.
  • To perform the essential functions of this position successful applicants must provide proof of U.S. citizenship, which is required to comply with federal regulations and contract.
  • Advanced knowledge of organizational change-management principles, methodologies, frameworks, tools, and best practices.
  • Significant experience designing and delivering OCM strategies for complex, enterprise-level, technology-enabled, process, organizational, or cultural changes.
  • Experience conducting change-impact, stakeholder, readiness, organizational, and change-risk assessments.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and execute communications, stakeholder engagement, sponsorship, training, coaching, resistance-management, and sustainment strategies.
  • Experience measuring and reporting adoption, readiness, engagement, proficiency, utilization, behavioral change, benefits realization, or other indicators of change effectiveness.
  • Experience supporting technology modernization, digital transformation, data and analytics initiatives, process improvement, automation, artificial intelligence, or other changes involving new tools and ways of working.
  • Excellent written, verbal, presentation, facilitation, consulting, negotiation, active-listening, and relationship-management skills.
  • Ability to translate complex technical, scientific, operational, or organizational information into clear, meaningful, and audience-appropriate messages.
  • Ability to establish and maintain strong relationships and work effectively with individuals and groups at all organizational levels and across diverse functional areas.
  • Ability to influence others, build coalitions, facilitate alignment, and move stakeholders toward a common vision or goal.
  • Ability to model Argonne’s Core Values: Impact, Safety, Respect, Integrity, and Teamwork.
  • Professional certification or formal training in organizational change management is preferred, e.g. Prosci, the Association of Change Management Professionals (ACMP).

title: Sr. Software Engineer
description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

Blue Origin is pioneering the future of space-based communications with TeraWave, a revolutionary satellite communications network designed to deliver symmetrical data speeds of up to 6 Tbps anywhere on Earth. This multi-orbit constellation will consist of optically interconnected satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) and medium Earth orbit (MEO), providing enterprise-grade connectivity for critical operations worldwide.

About This Role

Blue Origin is seeking a Senior Software Development Engineer to join the Software Engineering team supporting TeraWave in the Greater Seattle Area. In this role, you build the foundational platform infrastructure, the operating nervous system, deployed across TeraWave satellites, user terminals, and gateways. This position focuses on embedded Linux and low-level platform infrastructure, spanning fleet management, operating-system services, hardware integration, security, observability, and networking performance. You will shape reliable, high-performance systems that operate aboard LEO satellites. Responsibilities

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Design core Linux platform infrastructure, including process management, custom initialization systems, and inter-process communication frameworks.
  • Develop and maintain Linux kernel modules and device drivers to support custom hardware and platform requirements.
  • Modify kernel subsystems to improve scheduling, memory management, and I/O performance for embedded satellite systems.
  • Work with silicon, electrical, and RF teams to bring up hardware prototypes and optimize kernels for custom SoCs.
  • Debug system-level performance issues, minimize context switching, and tune the networking stack for satellite links.
  • Implement secure boot, runtime security monitoring, and hardware-backed credential management across embedded platforms.
  • Own the complete software lifecycle from architecture and development through deployment aboard LEO satellites.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, computer engineering, or related STEM discipline, or 10+ years software development experience.
  • At least 8 years of C or C++ experience in Linux or embedded environments.
  • Deep Linux kernel knowledge, including driver development, memory management, and system-level debugging.
  • Experience with system-level debugging tools such as GDB, perf, and eBPF.
  • Experience with Buildroot, Yocto, Bazel, or comparable build systems.
  • Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Preferred Qualifications

title: Principal NDE - Network & SDN - TeraWave
description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

Blue Origin is pioneering the future of space-based communications with TeraWave, a revolutionary satellite communications network designed to deliver symmetrical data speeds of up to 6 Tbps anywhere on Earth. This multi-orbit constellation will consist of optically interconnected satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) and medium Earth orbit (MEO), providing enterprise-grade connectivity for critical operations worldwide.

As a Principal Network Development Engineer for Network Architecture and SDN at TeraWave, you join the team responsible for the design and implementation of the "brain" of our constellation. We develop a dynamic, self-healing network that operates at orbital speeds across our multi-orbit constellation of 5,408 optically interconnected satellites. In this Principal role, you apply deep networking architecture expertise to develop critical components of our Ground and Terrestrial networking infrastructure. You collaborate with principal engineers and technical leaders to implement innovative approaches to routing, traffic management, and network resilience. This is a greenfield environment where you develop resilient, highly available, and secure ground networking connectivity that backhauls customer traffic.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Architect, develop, provision, and operate the terrestrial network across hundreds of global satellite gateway sites.

  • Define and evolve network architecture, engineering standards, and operational best practices for the global ground network.

  • Partner with network, cloud, and field engineering teams to deliver a scalable and resilient ground network.

  • Design automation frameworks and deployment pipelines that enable rapid, repeatable provisioning of complete gateway sites.

  • Integrate the satellite constellation with the terrestrial backbone across management, customer, and security networking services.

  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to engineers across multiple organizations on large-scale networking initiatives.

  • Drive architectural decisions and engineering excellence for successful delivery of complex ground network programs.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, related field, or equivalent experience.

  • 10 or more years of networking experience in large scale, complex production environments including WANs.

  • 7 or more years of technical leadership, architecture, design ownership, or mentorship in WAN environments.

  • Knowledge of BGP, IS-IS, OSPF, and Segment Routing (SRv6 or SR-MPLS) in network environments.

  • Experience with cloud networking, network virtualization, segmentation, and automation of large scale WAN architectures.

  • Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.

  • Experience designing highly available, fault tolerant, and robust WAN and ground network architectures.

  • Demonstrated ability to translate business needs into scalable, secure, reliable, and supportable network architecture decisions.

  • Ability to influence technical direction across multiple teams without relying on direct reporting authority.

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, strategic thinking, communication, and technical leadership skills.

  • Passion for Blue Origin's mission and ability to work in a fast paced, dynamic environment. Don't have all the listed qualifications? If you meet the basic qualifications and are excited about this role, we encourage you to apply.

title: Senior Network Engineer
description:
Competitive Range partners with the government to plan and deploy complex, IT-enabled, and mission-essential capabilities. Our goal is to help you develop and expand your professional capabilities while working on challenging, exciting projects in a collaborative, congenial environment.

Competitive Range Solutions requires the expertise of a talented and experienced Senior Network Engineer to assist in the direction and management of the program’s executive support group. The candidate must reference their ability and experience working in a Department of Defense (DoD) customer environment and effective integration with a government multi-contractor team.

The Senior Network Engineer will be critical in maintaining, troubleshooting, and enhancing our network infrastructure, focusing on urgent break-fixes and high-priority requirements. The candidate must have a deep understanding of network connectivity across various classification levels and be committed to excellent responses to incidents affecting mission-critical operations.

Roles and Responsibilities:

  • Actively participate in the Rapid Response Team to conduct urgent break-fixes and fulfill requirements in response to incidents. Prioritize and respond to incidents with the understanding that less than 5% of typical incidents are classified as urgent.
  • Manage network connectivity at all VIP/General Officer quarters within the scope of responsibility. Ensure readiness for VIP visits and support high-priority requirements in these locations.
  • Implement and manage network connectivity and transport across all classification levels. This includes managing and installing encryption devices, VoIP and VoSIP devices, and auxiliary power equipment (e.g., UPS).
  • Oversee life-cycle maintenance for all transport devices and supporting equipment. Ensure all installations, maintenance, and removals are conducted according to approved standards and architectural drawings.
  • Manage and perform patching and cabling for devices in VIP/GO quarters.
  • Assist the Crisis Management Teams in managing cost transfers and updating user agreements with the customer base.
  • Prepare the Rapid Response Team Monthly Report detailing work performed, including man-hours and materials spent supporting the month’s requirements.

Qualifications/Experience:

  • Active TS/SCI Clearance
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in network engineering, with a proven track record in rapid response and high-priority incident management.
  • Familiar with the duties of the JNOSC Core Engineering Team, Service Restoral Team, TACLANE Team, Service Response Team, and MAC Team.
  • Experience in managing network connectivity and transport across different classification levels.
  • Comprehensive knowledge of encryption devices, VoIP and VoSIP devices, and auxiliary power equipment.
  • Experience with patching and cabling network devices.

Education/Certifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in information systems, computer sciences, business management, or related field (Required)
  • Master's degree (Preferred)
  • One nationally recognized certification for senior network administrators/engineers/architects

title: Director, Clinical Research Alliances
description:
Job Description:

As a privately-owned, biopharmaceutical company, Ferring pioneers and delivers life-changing therapies that help people build families and live better lives. Our independence helps us cultivate an entrepreneurial spirit and long-term perspective that enables us to achieve growth and scale, while remaining agile and true to our ‘people first’ philosophy. Built on a 70-year plus commitment to science and research, Ferring is relentless in its pursuit of science that drives powerful discoveries and therapies to help people build families, stay healthy, and stand up to the world’s oldest enemy: disease.

As the Director, Clinical Research Alliances you will be responsible for aligning research objectives cross-functionally, both externally and internally, to achieve effective KOL engagement and support efficient study enrollment and trial completion.

With Ferring, you will be joining a recognized leader, identified as one of “The World’s Most Innovative Companies” by Fast Company, and honored by Fortune with inclusion on its “Change the World List,” for addressing society’s unmet needs. Ferring US is also Great Places to Work® Certified, distinguishing it as one of the best companies to work for in the country.

Responsibilities:

  • Contribute to and support the company’s efforts in communicating the high value of Ferring Uro-oncology research initiatives to successfully execute trial needs

  • Initiate and maintain relationships with study investigators to create advocates for Ferring Uro-Oncology research

  • Collaborate with the Therapeutic area medical team and medical affairs to support current PI involvement and KOL engagement initiatives

  • Uncover opportunities for engagement to ensure appropriate enrollment at each research center

  • Collaborate with Ferring clinical operations, TA medical directors, and CRO to identify and develop key performance indicators (KPIs) for activities aimed at enhancing trial recruitment, and ensure reports are developed and shared with management to track progress and drive improvements

  • Work with Ferring clinical operations, TA Medical Directors and CRO to understand KPIs for enrollment and support where necessary for optimal study performance – then delete this as incorporated in above

  • Work to facilitate collaboration between different departments or groups within the same study site to optimize the enrollment of trial participants, feeding back any trial-specific impact to the Ferring clinical operations team to ensure coordinated efforts

  • Report identified site or vendor issues to Clinical trial team via TA medical directors including opinions and observations related to the operational, scientific and other aspects of the study so that Ferring clinical operations team can assess appropriate trial-related actions

  • Collaborate with Ferring medical affairs and CTT during the start-up phase for selection of sites to enable and retain beneficial experiences and best practices

  • Ensure alignment of medical communications and publications plans within the overall medical brand and development plan – delete as this has too much overlap with existing teams and processes

  • Support and partner with key internal business partner

  • Ensure effective interaction & communication between the uro-oncology research team, medical science liaison teams and other key stakeholders

Requirements:
  • Previous experience that provides the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the job comparable to 15+ years in matrix leadership organizations in operational or client facing environments.
  • Minimum 5 years Uro-Oncology experience preferred
  • Bachelor’s degree; BSN or MBA strongly preferred.
  • Experience working with Urologist preferred
  • Prior medical affairs, medical communications, publications and/or KOL management experience highly desired
  • Proven leadership track record with exceptional communication, collaboration and prioritizing skills, supporting pre and post-launch activities.
  • Ability to analyze and summarize data, think critically, and manage multiple projects
  • Strong interpersonal skills including building and maintaining successful KOL and stakeholder relationships
  • Proven planning and organizational skills with experience managing multiple priorities; attention to detail and the ability to prioritize in a changing environment with a sense of urgency
  • Strong interpersonal skills in developing and maintaining professional relationships
  • Proven ability to collaborate across organizational boundaries
  • Proven success in driving cross functional teams toward a common goal and deliverables
  • Proficiency in project management
  • A high degree of self-motivation, organization, communication, and presentation skills; high competence in solving complex problems, as well as the ability to navigate a fast-paced cross functional and collaborative work environment
  • Ability to be independent, multitask and results oriented with hands-on attitude in a fast-paced and energetic environment
  • Excellent written and communication skills
  • Ability to think broadly about scientific communications and the impact on materials
  • Ability to develop collaborative relationships with internal colleagues including Global Medical Affairs leadership

Ferring + you

At Ferring, we offer competitive total compensation along with an exceptional range of flexible benefits, personal support and tailored learning and development opportunities all designed to help you realize your full potential both in life and at work. From working hours that respect your lifestyle, a culture that is welcoming and equitable, and the chance to work with the industry’s most impressive people, these are just some of the ways we live our "People First" philosophy.

Our Compensation and Benefits

At Ferring, base salary is one part of our competitive total compensation and benefits package and is determined using a salary range. The base salary range for this role is $178,000 to $210,000, which is the reasonable estimate of the base compensation for this role. The actual amount paid may differ based on non-discriminatory factors such as experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, education and primary work location. Additional compensation for this role will be provided based on competitive annual incentive compensation targets in the form of an annual bonus - payouts are based on individual and company performance.

Benefits for this role include: comprehensive healthcare (medical, dental, and vision) with a premium differential, inverse to base salary, to be paid by employees; a 401k plan and company match; short and long-term disability coverage; basic life insurance; wellness benefits; reimbursement for certain tuition expenses; sick time frontloaded yearly of 40 hours, or higher if state or local law requires; vacation time for full time employees to accrue between 112.5 and 150 hours yearly in the first four (4) years of employment, and additional accruals starting in the fifth (5th) year of employment; and 12 to 13 paid holidays per year. We are proud to offer 26 weeks of paid parental leave, learn more about the parental leave offering in our benefits package here. For roles that are not field-based, Ferring has a policy that allows employees to work up to two days from home and three at a Ferring site, weekly.

Ferring is an equal opportunity employer. All aspects of employment will be based on merit, competence, performance, and business needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of gender, race, color, religion, marital status, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other status protected under federal, state, or local laws.

Join our team and your voice will be heard, and your contributions will be valued. If you love to come up with new ways to make a positive difference and see them through, you will fit right in.

title: Senior Experience Design Lead
description:
About Northern Trust


As a global leader in innovative wealth management, asset servicing, asset management and banking services, Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS) is proud to guide the world’s most successful individuals, families, corporations and institutions.


Since 1889, we have aligned our efforts with our three guiding Principles That Endure: Service, Expertise, and Integrity. Together, they reflect the three cornerstones of business conduct which we strive to instill in our employees, whom we call partners, and to provide to our clients and the communities we serve worldwide.


With more than 135 years of financial experience and over 24,000 partners, we serve the world’s most sophisticated clients using leading technology and exceptional service.



Summary

The senior lead designer guides work in the Experience Design & Research practice, envisioning digital and service experiences for BU products and initiatives.
Senior lead designers tactically and strategically contribute to design and business objectives at varying stages of discovery, development, and delivery in collaboration with peers and stakeholders. They lead research for specific features and services in with their peers and counterparts in business and technology teams. They are responsible for differentiating experiences reflective of Northern Trust’s capabilities and business objectives as well as client and partner needs and behaviors.
Sr lead designers take responsibility for specific features or processes within a product or capability team, taking accountability for research activities or objectives with manageable risks and resource requirements. They act as a resource for colleagues with less experience.

Major Duties :

1. Works to improve user experiences with technology and business collaborators
2. Guides design to meet objectives and outcomes, influences business and technology decisions with user needs in mind
3. Contributes to an open culture that enables employees’ development through direct but kind feedback, promotes diverse perspectives and fosters a sense of curiosity and optimism
4. Creates user experiences, from low-fidelity sketches to high-fidelity mockups and prototypes while applying the NT Digital Design System.
5. Provides creative direction and conducts design reviews, balancing design decisions between research, technology, and business unit objectives
6. Solves complex problems and takes new perspectives on existing solutions
7. Exercises judgment based on the analysis of multiple sources of information
8. Works within broad guidelines and policies
9. May collaborate in an agile environment or ad hoc in emerging experience projects.
10. Guides designers and researchers relative to the current project or digital product

Knowledge :

• Ability to put Human-Centered Design and UI/UX best practices to work within a professional setting, as demonstrated in a work portfolio
• Proficiency in a range of relevant design methods and concepts, which may include low-fidelity sketching, information architecture, wireframe development, usability testing, research planning, competitive analysis
• Strong design skills in multiple competency areas (visual, interaction, information architecture, product)
• Able to present work and decisions effectively, through presentation and storytelling skills
• Ability to recognize, predict and incorporate use cases and user interactions into design
• Highly flexible, adaptable to change and comfortable with ambiguity and critique

• Experience working with design systems, using and managing Figma libraries.
• Effective use of collaborative/communication tools
• Clear growth mindset, looking for opportunities to learn and motivated to approach challenges proactively

Experience :

• 9+ years demonstrated work experience delivering digital experiences
• Educated in design or related field, formally or though comparable training
• Design thinking and UI/UX best practices, as demonstrated in a portfolio of professional work.
• Experience working with a cross-functional team or large-scale software development lifecycle, preferably in an agile environment, is desired

$114,500 - 194,700 USD

Salary range is a good faith estimate of base pay. Northern Trust provides a comprehensive benefits package including retirement benefits (401k and pension), health and welfare benefits (medical, dental, vision, spending accounts and disability), paid time off, parental and caregiver leave, life & accident insurance, and other voluntary and well-being benefits. title: Senior Staff Engineer, Systems Test (R5430)
description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

Job Description:

As a Software Systems Test Engineer, you will be pivotal in driving integration testing of our full aircraft software system, integrating our autonomy, flight controller, and GCS software to qualify an intelligent, robust aircraft system. This role demands an engineer capable of overseeing system-level verification and validation, designing complex test scenarios, and ensuring that subsystem testing meets rigorous standards before proceeding to full system integration. You will marshal our aircraft software through full system verification & validation. Your work will directly impact the reliability and performance of our aircraft, preparing them for operational excellence in the field.

What you'll do:

  • Generate detailed mission test scenarios that mimic real-world conditions to validate the performance of autonomy and flight control software.
  • Participate in design reviews for new features and design detailed test plans based on their requirements
  • Conduct and manage system verification and validation events, culminating in verified flight readiness.
  • Write test analyzers in Python to report and benchmark performance and qualification metrics of the system
  • Produce test coverage and release-readiness reports by aggregating test cases, results, and quality requirements
  • Recommend improvements to our simulation models and fault injection so that we can keep pushing the capabilities of our test suite before proceeding to flight

    • Required qualifications:

  • 10+ years of work experience in testing complex integrated software systems
  • Demonstrated expertise & experience in test automation, minimally writing software to automate testing, preferably leveraging simulation for automated integration testing
  • Strong experience with the software product development lifecycle, ideally for autonomy or vehicle systems
  • Great understanding of system architecture, requirement derivation, and test planning across the V-model
  • Experience with automating test cases in an existing test framework
  • Experience producing high-quality technical documentation, including test plans, quality-assurance reports, and operational procedures
  • Proven track record of successfully shipping products, showcasing the ability to navigate through development cycles, overcome obstacles, and deliver high-quality solutions to meet project deadlines and exceed expectations in a fast-paced environment
  • B.S., M.S, or PhD degree in Systems Engineering, Software Engineering, Computer Science or a related field

    • Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience with autonomous or robotic systems
  • Experience with simulation software and hardware emulation
  • Background in a fast-paced, R&D or startup environment
  • Proficiency in build test automation
  • Proficiency in Python or C++

description:

title: IRIS Self-Directed Personal Care (RN) (Milwaukee County, WI)
description:
Home Health Care, Hospice Care, Palliative Care, Long Term Care, Rehab

No weekends, No afterhours support, No holidays

Job Description

Job Summary

Are you seeking a unique nursing position that gives you a great work/life balance and lets you support people to live the lives that they choose? Then you’ll want to keep reading about this rewarding work opportunity!

We are currently looking for a Registered Nurse licensed in Wisconsin to become our next IRIS Self-Directed Personal Care (SDPC) RN. This is a remote position, where you will partner with people in your community who are enrolled in the Wisconsin IRIS program – a Medicaid long-term care option for older adults and people with disabilities. People in the IRIS program who need personal care services have the choice to enroll in the IRIS Self-Directed Personal Care (IRIS SPDC) option. You can learn more about IRIS SDPC on the Wisconsin Department of Health Services website here, and learn about the IRIS program here. While this role is home-based, you will have regularly scheduled visits with people in their homes and communities.

As an IRIS SDPC RN, you’ll provide oversight and guidance to the people enrolled in the IRIS SDPC option. You’ll also build relationships with the people you partner with and ensure that they’re getting the most out of the IRIS Self-Directed Personal Care option through assessment, oversight, training and education.

IRIS SDPC RNs are responsible for administering the Wisconsin Personal Care Screening Tool; creating person-centered plans of care; providing personal care oversight to a group of people in IRIS, providing education and training for IRIS participants and care providers, and conducting the required documentation and follow-up. As an IRIS SDPC RN, you’ll play an important role in helping people of various backgrounds and abilities live their lives the way they choose.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

  • Provides personal care assessments and oversight to the My Cares Groups by administering the Wisconsin Personal Care Screening Tool and addendums as required
  • Documents assessment as required by individual tool and Department of Health Services policies and by completing oversight visits and calls as required
  • Oversees a My Cares Groups of participants, develops individual plans of care, ensures physician orders for care are obtained and reviews and revises plan of care as needed
  • Submits for Prior Authorization for personal care services
  • Complies with all Department of Health Services policies and SDPC Guidelines, procedures, and practices along with documentation and program regulations
  • Provides personal care training to participants or care providers as requested and provides educational materials as needed
  • Completes collateral contacts with IRIS Consultants and Long-Term Care Functional Screeners and physicians to ensure care needs are met
  • Completes other duties as assigned
  • Overtime work may be required
  • May be required to drive 50% of the time during a given day of member home visits
  • Exposure to members homes which may include navigating stairs, exposure to different environments, and pets

    Required Qualifications
    • At least 2 years nursing experience, and at least 1 year of experience serving the target groups of the IRIS program (adults with physical/intellectual disabilities or older adults), or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
    • Active and unrestricted Registered Nurse (RN) license in the state of Wisconsin.
    • Associate's degree in nursing.
    • Valid and unrestricted driver's license, reliable transportation, and adequate auto insurance for job related travel requirements unless otherwise required by law.
    • Database operation/maintenance skills and data entry experience.
    • Teaching and mentoring skills.
    • Analytical and problem-solving skills.
    • Strong organizational and time-management skills, and ability to manage tasks independently.
    • Flexibility in the work environment, and willingness and ability to adapt to changing organizational needs.
    • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
    • Microsoft Office suite/applicable software program(s) proficiency.

    Preferred Qualifications
    • Experience providing care through the Wisconsin Medical Assistance Personal Care program (MPAC).
    • Home care/home health experience.

title: Shift Leader – Additive Manufacturing Post-Processing – C Shift
description:

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

As part of a hardworking team of C & D-shift technicians and machinists you will lead the team in all aspects of Additive Manufacturing Post-Processing, consisting of powder removal, support removal, EDM machining, tensile turning/testing, inspection, and various other tasks related to manufacturing.

Special Mentions

- Relocation provided

- Friday - Sunday 5am to 530pm

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

- Lead and develop a team of post-processing technicians and machinists across the C/D shift; set priorities, assign work, manage break coverage, and ensure safe, compliant operations.

- Coordinate priorities with manufacturing engineers, planners, and quality to meet build plans and promise dates.

- Proactively identify and remove blockers (e.g., nonconformances, stop-work, missing tools/fixtures, document errors).

- Enforce safety policies for metal AM post-processing (powders, fumes, sharp edges, lockout/tagout, machine guarding, ergonomics).

- Sustain 5S/visual management and ensure compliance with procedures, work instructions, and certifications (e.g., ISO/AS quality systems).

- Stage additive manufactured (AM) hardware for outplant processing, collaborating with material handlers, shipping, and receiving teams to coordinate expedited (HOT) shipments and ensure timely delivery

- Coordinate with external vendors to resolve certification requirements and purchase order (PO) discrepancies, maintaining accurate documentation and compliance standards

- Perform comprehensive quality control activities including visual inspections, surface finish evaluations, scrap hardware, and complex borescope operations to ensure parts meet specifications

- Demonstrate understanding of end-to-end manufacturing processes from raw material procurement through inventory management, with ability to identify and propose process improvements

- Maintain accurate inventory records and tracking systems for AM components

- Support non-conformance reporting and corrective action processes

- Collaborate with engineering teams on design feedback and manufacturability assessments

- Ensure compliance with aerospace quality standards (AS9100, etc.)

- Participate in continuous improvement initiatives and lean manufacturing practices

- Provide technical support for production issues and troubleshooting

Minimum Qualifications

- High school diploma or GED.

- 5+ years’ hands-on experience in manufacturing operations

- 1–3+ years leading technicians or machinists on off-shift operations (C/D or equivalent), or in a lead/supervisor capacity.

- Proficiency reading engineering drawings and interpreting GD&T; experience with in-process inspection and documentation.

- Working knowledge of EDMs, bandsaws, and basic machining practices; familiarity with tensile specimen preparation is a plus.

- Strong communication, prioritization, and problem-solving skills in a fast-paced, safety-critical environment.

- Ability to stand for extended periods and lift up to 50 lbs; comfortable using PPE and operating in a metal AM post-processing environment.

- Willingness to work nights/weekends and overtime as needed to support schedule.

- Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with metal AM materials/processes

- Prior ownership of cell metrics (throughput, FPY, scrap/rework, cycle time, OTD) with demonstrated improvements.

- Familiarity with AS9100 or similar quality systems.

- Lean/continuous improvement experience (5S, standard work, kaizen, visual management).

- Ability to obtain a forklift certification.

WA applicants is $113,158.00 - $158,420.85

Other site ranges may differ

title: Presales Engineer (LMR - Central Region)
description:
Company Overview

At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.


Department Overview

The Sales Engineering Group is the technical lifeblood of the sales organization. Our engineers bring to life the innovative communications solutions that make a difference in the moments that matter. The Sales Engineering groups have the technology and design responsibility for all sales support engagements within the region. This position is within the T5 (Midwest) Projects Presale Engineering Team.


Job Description

The Presales Engineer is the architect and owner of the solution design. You will be responsible for working closely with the Sales Team to deliver customer driven, world class, leading edge, end-to-end solutions that rise to the challenges of first responder agencies within the territory. The team concentrates on the following mission-critical communications technologies at various levels of complexity: Public Safety grade mobile/portable voice and data networks, Advanced Mobile devices, Public Safety mobile broadband networks and devices (LTE), Integrated Command & Control: 9-1-1 Dispatch Consoles, Mobile Video, Cybersecurity and more. This person will work closely with the Area Sales Manager and Presale Business Manager to understand, manage, and prioritize the presale opportunities within the Midwest region.

Responsibilities:

  • Coordination with the various functional teams (Systems Integration, Service, Sales, Product Groups) to ensure all business unit goals are addressed in our proposals and win-strategies

  • Development of the implementation approach and service plan necessary to win the project

  • Meeting/exceeding customer requirements and providing value alternatives when requirements cannot be met

  • Managing to support Motorola’s sales, revenue, and margin goals

  • Driving all sole source & RFP (Request for Proposal) projects to completion

  • Collaborating with project team members (engineering, proposal specialist, sales, and service) in the development of proposed solutions

  • Working with 3rd party vendors as needed to develop fully integrated solutions

  • Responsible for being the technical solution owner of budgetary, competitive, and sole source proposal responses

  • Assists in providing point by point technical responses to Request for Proposal (RFP) and Request for Information (RFI) responses

  • Provide hardware and software recommendations based on customer requirements

  • Provide solutions description and system configuration diagrams

  • Provide bill of material for software, hardware, and non-standard third party applications

  • Identify interface requirements and solicit system implementation team for design

  • Conduct customer facing technical requirements discovery sessions for estimation and configuration (Conference Call or In Person)

  • Builds relationships with sales, internal engineering, system integration, proposal, pricing, and key technical subject matter expert teams within the organization

  • Work with the customer and the sales team to deploy product evaluations as necessary

  • Ability to provide customer product training (both in-person and virtual)

  • Computer hardware sizing, configuration and implementation experience

  • Technical writing experience and the ability to deliver technical information to a nontechnical audience

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree with 4+ years of experience in one or more of the following: Sales, Engineering, Public Safety, and/or Solutions Architecture

  • OR 4+ years of experience in one or more of the following: Sales, Engineering, Public Safety, and/or Solutions Architecture

  • Ability to build strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders

  • Willingness to think out of the box and challenge the status quo

  • Strong general knowledge of wireless communications fundamentals and voice/data architectures - both public and private (e.g. APCO P25, LTE, 802.11, 3G/4G) is highly desirable.

title: Scientist Intern, User Experience (HCI/HMI)
description:
Charles River Analytics, a GRVTY company, creates solutions and technology to tackle the world’s most challenging problems. Our team of technological entrepreneurs works together to push at the forefront of enhanced AI, robotics, smart sensing, and human-centered computing. The resulting research and development help to continuously advance government programs and discover new possibilities in the commercial marketplace. At Charles River, we take great pride in our success at attracting and retaining the most talented and creative problem-solvers in our field. Now as part of GRVTY, we offer the same trusted capabilities with increased organizational depth and expanded capacity across mission-critical national security domains. Are you ready to accelerate our mission-focused innovations? We’d love to hear from you!

Our interns work on real projects and cutting-edge technology. We believe strongly in promoting within, which is demonstrated by the fact that we not only have hired former interns, but that several of our senior-level staff began their careers at Charles River as interns!

We are looking for an enthusiastic Scientist Intern for our UX Innovation division. We are seeking students with an interest in learning about how to build human-centered systems and a successful academic background in the following areas: human factors, cognitive systems engineering, human computer interaction, user interface (UI) and user experience (UX) design/assessment, and quantitative/qualitative data analysis.

You will use a variety of approaches such as: knowledge elicitation, task analysis, iterative user-centered design approaches, and human factors-based usability evaluation methods. During your time at Charles River, you will work in small project-oriented groups of scientists and software engineers to address challenging problems related to creating user-centered technology and cognitive-support tools.

What we're looking for:

  • In pursuit of a PhD in Computer Science, Human Factors, or related field
  • Experience with user experience, human-computer interaction, or human factors
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently as well as effectively within a team environment
  • Strong verbal and written skills to support report writing
  • U.S. citizenship

Not required, but we’d love to see:

  • Requirements analysis
  • Quantitative and/or qualitative data analysis
  • Wireframing and concept design
  • Usability and/or technology evaluation

$20.00 - $30.00 per hour

The final salary will be decided after careful evaluation of the individual's work experience, education, and overall qualifications. This range does not include the substantial total rewards, as listed below, that you will also be eligible for as an employee owner at Charles River Analytics.

title: Social- og sundhedsassistent og social- og sundhedshjælper i primær dagvagt
description:
Hjemmeplejen Nord, Struer Kommune

Brænder du for dit fag, og motiveres du af at gøre en forskel for borgerne i deres eget hjem?

Har du lyst til at være en del af et lille, engageret og tværfagligt team, hvor vi hjælper hinanden og har fokus på både faglighed, trivsel og arbejdsglæde? Så er det måske dig, vi søger.

Vi søger en social- og sundhedsassistent og en social- og sundhedshjælper til Hjemmeplejen Nord, Struer Kommune, Rolighedsvej 1, 7790 Hvidbjerg, Thyholm.

  • Stillingerne er som udgangspunkt i dagvagt på 37 timer ugentligt eller efter ønske.
  • Der arbejdes hver 2. weekend, og der er mulighed for enkelte aftenvagter, hvis du ønsker det.
  • Stillingerne ønskes besat den 1. oktober 2026 – gerne tidligere, hvis det er muligt.


Hvem er du?

Vi forestiller os, at du:

  • er uddannet social- og sundhedsassistent eller social- og sundhedshjælper
  • har lyst til at være en del af et lille tværfagligt team
  • er nysgerrig på den nye ældrelov og arbejdet med helhedspleje
  • arbejder selvstændigt, engageret og ansvarsfuldt
  • har blik for borgerens egne ressourcer, ønsker og muligheder
  • er åben for at udvikle og udvide dine kompetencer
  • har gode samarbejdsevner og bidrager positivt til fællesskabet
  • møder borgerne og dine kollegaer med godt humør
  • har kørekort

Du får en grundig introduktionsperiode, og der er altid mulighed for yderligere oplæring.

Hvem er vi, og hvad kan vi tilbyde?

Vi er et hjemmeplejeområde med ét team, som arbejder tæt og tværfagligt sammen med terapeuter og sygeplejersker.

Vi er godt på vej med implementeringen af helhedspleje og arbejder med afsæt i borgerens ønsker, ressourcer og livskvalitet.

Vores arbejdsområde er Thyholm og området lige syd for Oddesundbroen.

Hos os får du:

  • en arbejdsplads, hvor arbejdsglæde og trivsel vægtes højt
  • gode kollegaer med forskellige fagligheder
  • et tæt tværfagligt samarbejde
  • mulighed for faglig udvikling og oplæring
  • en hverdag med åbenhed, humor og plads til forskellighed
  • mulighed for at være med til at udvikle helhedsplejen

Vi arbejder ud fra vores kerneopgave:
”At borgeren i relationen med os oplever selvbestemmelse, værdighed og livskvalitet.”

Praktiske oplysninger

Løn- og ansættelsesvilkår følger gældende overenskomst.

Vil du gerne vide mere om stillingerne, er du velkommen til at kontakte funktionsleder Birgit Thusholt Gøtzsche på telefon 24 29 25 13 eller mail btg@struer.dk.

Ansøgningsfristen er mandag den 24. august 2026 kl. 8.00.

Ansættelsessamtaler kan blive afholdt løbende.

Lyder det som noget for dig? Så glæder vi os til at modtage din ansøgning.

Struer Kommune opfordrer alle kvalificerede ansøgere uanset alder, køn, religion, eller etnisk tilhørsforhold at søge.

Det er en forudsætning for ansættelsen, at du er indstillet på at anvende dit eget MitID i forbindelse med varetagelsen af jobbet. MitID bruges udelukkende til nødvendige arbejdsrelaterede godkendelser og administrative processer.

Hvem er vi?
I Struer Kommune er det opgaven, der sætter holdet. Det er din faglighed og gode dømmekraft, der skal være fundamentet for det samspil, du skaber med borgeren og virksomhederne.
Sammen skaber vi stærke partnerskaber og er fælles om at udvikle fremtidens velfærd. Men hvad er fremtidens velfærd? Vi har ikke svarende alene. Derfor skal vi have medarbejdere, der sætter spørgsmålstegn og borgere og virksomheder, som udfordrer. Vi stiller krav til os selv, men vi forventer ligeledes noget af borgerne og virksomhederne. Gode løsninger kommer, når alle bidrager til fællesskabet.

Læs mere om Struer Kommune

Lydens By
Vi er Lydens By. Lyden er en inspirationskilde til nye projekter og initiativer, der kan realisere kommunens vækstpotentialer og styrkepositioner til et lokalsamfund, som mennesker har lyst til at besøge, arbejde og bo i.

For os er det naturligt at vores byudvikling tager udgangspunkt i lyd, og vores kunstværker bruger lyden aktivt. Vi arbejder med, hvordan lyd påvirker livskvaliteten positivt hos demente, indlæring hos børn eller fraværet af lyd skaber arbejdsglæde.

Lyd er i vores DNA.Læs mere om vores visioner og strategier.

Går du med flyttetanker?
Du har lyst til at søge ovenstående stilling, men er lidt i tvivl om, hvilke muligheder du har for at flytte til? Måske er det nødvendigt, at din partner også finder job i området? Struer Kommune har en Tilflytterservice, hvor du eller din partner ganske gratis og uforpligtende kan få direkte og personlig hjælp, hvis du går med overvejelser om at flytte til Struer. Kontakt Tilflytterservice på tilflytterservice@struer.dk

title: Pædagog til Specialinstitutionen Magnoliahuset
description:
Magnoliahuset søger 1 fast pædagog på 37 timer pr. 1 september 2026 eller snarest derefter.

Vi er et specialiseret dagtilbud under Barnets lov §82/§83. Målgruppen er 34 børn i alderen 0- 6 år, med psykiske funktionsnedsættelser og/eller fysiske funktionsnedsættelser.

Børnene i Magnoliahuset har diagnoser indenfor autismespektret (ASF), - forskellige syndromer, - ADHD, - motoriske / fysiske funktionsnedsættelser eller andre diagnoser. Det kan også være børn uden diagnose, som er forsinkede i deres udvikling. Fælles for børnene er, at de alle profiterer af at være i et specialpædagogisk miljø, med tæt voksen kontakt.

Vi tager altid udgangspunkt i barnets nærmeste udviklingszone og arbejder ud fra en TEACCH inspireret tilgang, hvor forudsigelighed og struktur er altafgørende. Desuden anvender vi flere pædagogiske metoder og teoretiske tilgange, herunder; Intensiv Interaktion, Marte Meo, Theraplay, visuelle kommunikationssystemer, talemaskiner og sanse motorik.

Vores åbningstid er fra kl. 6.30 til kl. 17.00 alle hverdage.

Vi søger en pædagog som:

  • har erfaring og viden om specialområdet eller lysten til at sætte sig ind i det.
  • har kendskab til børns generelle udviklingsstadier i alderen 0-6 år.
  • kan indgå i et fagligt reflekterende samarbejde med kollegaer, konsulenter og ledelsen.
  • kan forholde sig nysgerrigt og åbent til samarbejdet med forældre.
  • formår at formulere sig skriftligt på et fagligt højt niveau, og er tryg ved digitale redskaber.
  • kan bidrage til at skabe struktur og forudsigelighed for det enkelte barn og i gruppen af børn.
  • er udviklingsorienteret, nærværende og vil bidrage aktivt og engageret i samarbejdet med kollegaer og ledelsen.

Vi tilbyder:

  • en spændende arbejdsplads med årlig udviklingsdag og mulighed for at deltage i relevante faglige konferencer.
  • en faglig stærk og reflekterende personalegruppe.
  • et tæt samarbejde og faglig sparring med kollegaer, ledelsen og konsulenter - så som psykolog, ergoterapeut, fysioterapeut samt logopæd.
  • supervision i grupper på tværs af huset med tilknyttet psykolog.
  • møder med plads til refleksion
  • 1 times forberedelsestid hver uge

Løn og ansættelse:

Løn og ansættelsesvilkår i henhold til gældende overenskomst, og efter principperne i Ny løn. Der skal indhentes straffeattest og børneattest ved ansættelse i Frederiksberg kommune.

Magnoliahuset er en røgfri arbejdsplads.

Yderligere oplysninger fås ved at kontakte Institutionsleder Karen Kloch Møller eller souschef Birgitte Munch Jensen på tlf.: 38 21 17 80.

Vores institutionsbeskrivelse kan læses på Magnoliahusets hjemmeside.

https://frb-magnoliahuset.aula.dk

Ansøgningsfrist er søndag d. 16. august 2026. Vi afholder løbende samtaler fra uge 33.

Skriftlig ansøgning skal foretages digitalt, vedlagt kopi af eksamenspapir m.v.


Frederiksberg er en levende by med et dynamisk bysamfund. Byens sjæl bygger på vores historie og klassiske arv og er med til at præge den spændende udvikling af Frederiksberg som en grøn, sund og pulserende del af Hovedstaden.
Vi er en moderne kommune, der betjener 104.305 borgere. Frederiksberg Kommune ønsker at fremme ligestillingen og opfordrer derfor alle kvalificerede til at søge uanset alder, handicap, race, hudfarve, religion eller tro, politisk anskuelse, seksuel orientering, kønsidentitet, kønsudtryk eller kønskarakteristika eller national, social eller etnisk oprindelse.

title: Term Project and Event Coordinator: Prenatal-to-3 Policy Impact Center
description:
Prenatal-to-3 Policy Impact Center – Project and Event Coordinator

Job Description Summary:

The Prenatal-to-3 Policy Impact Center aims to accelerate states’ equitable implementation of evidence-based policies that help all children thrive from the start. The Center’s policy team includes three distinct, but closely-connected functions related to the Center’s state-level policy expertise, analysis, and support for states: policy research, state policy, and state relations. The policy team’s state relations team shapes policy action through strategic engagement and relationship building with state leaders and national partners. We are seeking a highly organized, detail-oriented project and event coordinator to support the overall work of the state relations team and collaborate across teams and the Center to manage external presentations and coordinate Center-hosted events. Candidates should have experience seamlessly managing the logistics of concurrent events.

General Notes:

This position reports functionally and administratively to the State Relations Manager. Applicants from underrepresented groups are encouraged to apply. We are committed to building an inclusive and diverse environment to continue to build a strong and equitable prenatal-to-3 system of care. Visa sponsorship is unavailable for this position. Candidates must be local to the Nashville area. This position is eligible for a hybrid work schedule that includes both remote and in-office work. This position is a 12-month term appointment beginning upon date of hire.

The primary responsibilities of the position include:

Project and event coordination:

  • Support Policy Impact Center-hosted webinar and event/meeting planning, including:

  • Keeping all event logistics including date, time, location, audience, content, and need for/management of printed materials on track with detailed event planning timelines and checklists

  • Providing virtual and on-site support including supporting the creation and execution of the run of show for both virtual and in-person events; serving as on-site lead for all in-person events and meetings; coordinating panelists and tech rehearsals for virtual events; serving as point of contact for attendees at virtual events; coordinating printing and shipping of materials as needed)

  • Serve as point of contact through clear, responsive, and professional communication with external partners requesting presentations, collecting necessary details and timelines to share with Center staff

  • Share informed recommendations to Center staff for site planning and logistics including event location and space needs, and coordinating catering selections, materials, printing, technology and AV, and décor, and other related needs

  • Communicate and coordinate across the Center’s teams to manage event details including with the operations teams on budget, contracting, and logistics, and the communications team for event promotion and production and other teams as required for agenda and content development

  • Manage tracking and internal coordination of Center staff’s external presentations

  • Support post-event follow-up and surveys to collect information for continuous improvement efforts

  • Troubleshoot logistics challenges in timely and professional manner.

  • Provide exemplary customer service, including with external partners and event attendees.

  • Perform clerical tasks, including writing, editing, and formatting documents and other communications; data entry and retrieval; scheduling and task management; printing event materials

  • Demonstrate ownership for event timelines, tracking, and all work products and processes

  • Perform other related functions as assigned

Supervisory Relationships:

This position does not have supervisory responsibility.

Required/Essential qualifications:

  • Previous experience managing the logistics of virtual and in-person events, including coordinating multiple events simultaneously while keeping detailed records and timelines organized

  • Excellent project management and organizational skills with meticulous attention to detail

  • Ability to multi-task effectively, including coordinating concurrent events and produce high-quality work under time constraints

  • Competency working under deadline pressure and adapting to changes in workload or timelines.

  • Excellent interpersonal skills, customer service, and verbal and written communication skills, including experience communicating with senior-level professionals.

  • Experience working independently and collaboratively as circumstances dictate

  • Creative thinking and problem-solving skills.

  • Experience using virtual event and CRM platforms (e.g., Zoom Webinar and Hubspot) for registration, communications, and event execution

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office products including Microsoft Outlook, experience with Microsoft Excel for production of event materials (e.g., mail merge), and an ability to learn new procedures and applications

  • Demonstrated understanding and support for key concepts in diversity, equity, and inclusion; and commitment to valuing diversity and contributing to an inclusive working and learning environment

  • Ability to travel by air approximately three times per year, generally for one to four nights.

  • Must be located in the Nashville area and able to come into the office or event sites in the metro area as needed

  • High school diploma or its equivalent, plus five years of progressively more complex administrative experience

Commitment to Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion

At Vanderbilt University, we are intentional about and assume accountability for fostering advancement and respect for equity, diversity, and inclusion for all students, faculty, and staff. Our commitment to diversity makes us who we are. We have created a community that celebrates differences and lets individuality thrive. As part of this commitment, we actively value diversity in our workplace and learning environments as we seek to take advantage of the rich backgrounds and abilities of everyone. The diverse voices of Vanderbilt represent an invaluable resource for the University in its efforts to fulfill its mission and strive to be an example of excellence in higher education.

Vanderbilt University is an equal opportunity, affirmative action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Please note, all candidates selected for an offer of employment are subject to pre-employment background checks, which may include but are not limited to, based on the role for which they have been selected: criminal history, education verification, social media review, motor vehicle records, credit history, and professional license verification.

title: Airside Experience Specialist - HNL
description:
As an Airside Experience Specialist, you are the face of our private aviation terminal, delivering a seamless, personalized, and welcoming experience for every guest, crew member, and aircraft in our care. In this dynamic role, you'll combine exceptional hospitality with hands-on operational support to ensure our guests feel cared for, from wheels down to wheels up.

You’ll operate ground service equipment and perform aircraft ground services while engaging guests with professionalism and a service-first mindset. This role requires schedule flexibility, including nights, weekends and holidays, and the ability to thrive in outdoor environments around active aircraft and in varying weather conditions.

If you enjoy creating memorable guest experiences in a fast-paced, luxury-driven environment – and you're excited by the energy of the runway – this is the role for you.

(Other duties may be assigned)

  • Work as part of a team to conduct airside operations safely and efficiently in accordance with established policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs) ensuring efficient and accurate communication through various methods to accomplish operational tasks.
  • Collaborate, cooperate, and work closely with all team members, guests, clients, vendors, and aircraft crewmembers to ensure service needs are met. Services include, but are not limited to, fueling, de-icing, lavatory, ground power and potable water services, parking, marshalling, wing walking, delivering catering and towing.
  • Proactively prepare for arriving/departing aircraft, identify and perform open job tasks, and immediately speak up and/or point out observed safety concerns to all stakeholders.

  • Follow emergency response procedures during critical events.
  • Understand, comply with, and enforce all security (physical, cyber and data) protocols as dictated by both Signature Aviation and the airport.
  • Create accurate records pertaining to time worked and activities and services performed.

Minimum Education and/or Experience:

  • High School Diploma or General Education Degree (GED).
  • Minimum of 18 years of age.
  • Ability to pass company background checks (criminal and motor vehicle), drug tests, meet airport background check requirements to receive and maintain an airport security badge, and be insurable by the Company's applicable insurance policies.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the jurisdiction of employment.
  • Excellent vision and coordination to move and/or direct aircraft and visually inspect aircraft fuel. Ability to pass a color vision test for purposes of inspecting aviation fuel.
  • Must possess a valid state driver’s license. In some locations a commercial driver’s license (CDL) is required as dictated by local regulations and business needs.
  • Must be able to exercise good judgment and follow directions/directives from supervisor/management.
  • Preferred: Three (3) to six (6) months experience and/or training in aviation, customer service or other related field; or equivalent combination of education and experience and/or training.

Additional knowledge and essential skills:

  • Hospitality Skills: Excellent guest service skills with an energetic, outgoing, and guest-obsessed personality. Must be able to anticipate guest needs and prioritize guest requests and job responsibilities by exhibiting a keen ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment. Must be able to maintain professionalism and confidentiality.
  • Language Skills: Ability to read and comprehend documents such as safety rules, operating instructions, and procedure manuals, and for safety-sensitive tasks, in English. Clearly communicate in English with others in person, via telephone, radio communicators, and in writing.
  • Math Skills: Ability to perform simple arithmetic (e.g., addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, percentages, fractions, angles, degrees, time).
  • Physical Ability: Must be able to physically enter/exit and operate motor vehicles and ground support equipment such as fuel trucks, vans, tugs, and cars. Must be able to perform various functions safely and efficiently (e.g., fueling, de-icing) from elevated heights.
  • Critical Thinking / Reasoning Ability: Ability to carry out multi-step instructions. Ability to deal with standardized situations with only occasional or no variables.
  • Interpersonal Skills: Ability to get along and work well with others. Excellent interpersonal skills for effective collaboration with team members and service to guests.
  • Multitasking: Ability to handle multiple tasks simultaneously while maintaining attention to detail.
  • Computer Skills: Ability to use a computer and email, learn necessary company software, and pass computer-based training modules.

  • Task Management: Ability to successfully and timely complete Signature’s training programs.

    Pay ranges vary based on multiple factors, including, without limitation, skill sets, education, shift worked, responsibilities, seniority, geographical market, merit, output, productivity, prior training or experience, and travel. The pay range for this position is $20.03 to $25.04 / hour.

description:
• Competitive hourly rate

Start your career in farming - join our supportive team on Souters Dairy

The Opportunity

Are you keen to give farming a go, or maybe you have some farming experience, and you are looking for some casual work.

We are looking for someone to start asap, to cover some leave on farm, and in the long run you may be happy to help on farm from time to time. You’ll get out and do general farm duties like milking, calf-rearing, fencing, spraying weeds. You will have a supportive team environment and training provided.

• A good eye for detail and a willingness to learn

• Restricted or full driver’s licence

Souters Dairy Farm is a well-managed operation within our Weka Complex on the West Coast, known for its structured systems and established processes.

Located just ten minutes from Lake Brunner and thirty minutes from Greymouth, this 483-hectare property milks 840 cows through a modern 50-bail rotary shed equipped with automatic cup removers (ACRs) and an in-shed feeding system.

You’ll be well supported and will benefit by learning from others. We offer a competitive hourly rate.

Vi leder efter en medarbejder, der naturligt tager ansvar, arbejder struktureret og har blik for både detaljen og helheden. Du motiveres af at hjælpe andre, kan bevare overblikket i en travl hverdag og følger dine opgaver helt til dørs.

  • Koordinere og planlægge opgaver for vores servicemedarbejdere.

  • Journalisering og øvrige administrative opgaver.

  • Følge op på henvendelser og sikre, at beboerne får den bedst mulige service.

  • Understøtte den daglige drift af lokalkontoret med forskellige administrative opgaver.

  • er serviceminded og møder mennesker med et smil og en professionel tilgang.

  • arbejder struktureret og kan prioritere dine opgaver.

  • tager ansvar og trives med selvstændigt arbejde.

  • har gode samarbejds- og kommunikationsevner.

Hos MS Bolig bliver du en del af en arbejdsplads, hvor samarbejde, hjælpsomhed og en uformel omgangstone præger hverdagen. Vi tilbyder:

  • en fast fuldtidsstilling på 37 timer.

  • løn og ansættelsesvilkår efter gældende overenskomst.

About JLL

Our people at JLL are shaping the future of real estate for a better world by combining world-class services, advisory, and technology for our clients. Whether you've got deep experience in commercial real estate, skilled trades or technology, or you're looking to apply your relevant experience to a new industry, join our team as we help shape a brighter way forward.

Role Overview

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you will operate at the front lines of innovation — embedded directly with subject matter experts, product, and engineering teams to rapidly design, architect, prototype, and deploy solutions that solve high-priority business problems. This is not a traditional engineering role with long delivery cycles. You will be expected to go from concept to working prototype in days, not months, while maintaining enterprise-grade standards for quality, security, and scalability.

You bring an exceptional combination of skills: deep hands-on engineering experience across AI agents and full-stack development, and the interpersonal skills to earn trust, drive alignment, and influence without authority. You are equally comfortable whiteboarding a system architecture with senior stakeholders and writing production code the same afternoon. You thrive in fast, ambiguous environments where creative thinking and execution speed matter, and you're also a dependable partner when production systems need attention.

Key Responsibilities

Solution Design & Architecture
  • Lead solution design for complex, cross-functional data and AI problems — from initial discovery through to technical blueprint
  • Define and communicate architecture decisions, trade-offs, and delivery approaches to both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Design scalable, modular systems that balance the need for speed with enterprise standards for reliability, security, and maintainability
  • Participate in architecture reviews, ensuring alignment with enterprise patterns and platform standards
  • Create clear technical documentation: architecture diagrams, data flow maps, API contracts, and solution briefs
Rapid Prototyping & Solution Delivery
  • Design and deliver working prototypes for complex data and AI problems within compressed timeframes, often days to weeks
  • Translate ambiguous business requirements into concrete technical solutions with minimal hand-holding
  • Balance speed of delivery with enterprise standards — your prototypes are production-ready, not throwaway
  • Continuously iterate on solutions based on direct feedback from product managers, program leads, and end users
  • Develop intuitive front-end interfaces and dashboards that bring data and AI outputs to life for business users
AI Agent Development
  • Design, build, and deploy AI agents and multi-agent systems that automate complex workflows end-to-end
  • Develop and maintain agent skills — discrete, reusable capabilities that compose into larger agentic pipelines
  • Implement and extend Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and clients to connect AI agents with enterprise tools, APIs, and data sources
  • Design evaluation harnesses, guardrails, and monitoring pipelines to ensure agent reliability and safety in production
  • Stay current with the rapidly evolving agentic AI landscape and proactively introduce new techniques and tooling to the team
  • Integrate LLMs, RAG systems, and ML models into production workflows
Application Support & Operational Reliability
  • Serve as a technical point of contact for production issues across deployed AI and data applications, triaging and resolving incidents promptly
  • Monitor application health, respond to alerts, and coordinate with platform and infrastructure teams to maintain SLA commitments
  • Contribute to post-incident reviews, identify root causes, and implement preventive measures to reduce recurrence
  • Maintain runbooks and operational documentation so that support responsibilities are scalable and transferable across the team
Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement
  • Embed directly with product, program, and engineering teams to co-define problems and co-deliver solutions
  • Influence technical direction and build alignment across teams without relying on formal authority
  • Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical business stakeholders — in writing, in meetings, and in executive presentations
  • Mentor and elevate junior engineers, sharing patterns and practices for agentic development, prompt design, and rapid delivery
  • Foster a collaborative, low-ego team culture where speed and quality go hand in hand

Qualifications

Critical Skills
  • Years of professional software engineering experience proportional to level, including solution design and architecture ownership
  • Demonstrated ability to architect end-to-end systems — from requirements through deployment — with clear documentation and stakeholder communication
  • Hands-on experience building AI agents, including defining agent skills, tool use, memory, and multi-step reasoning
  • Experience with AI-Augmented Engineering — actively using tools like Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or equivalent assistants to accelerate coding, documentation, and problem-solving day-to-day
  • Direct experience with AWS Agent Core, Azure AI Foundry, Google Vertex AI Agents, or equivalent production agent infrastructure — building, deploying, and operating agents in production
  • Working knowledge of Model Context Protocol (MCP) — including building or consuming MCP servers to connect agents with external systems
  • Experience with agentic frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, or Semantic Kernel
  • Proficiency in Python and at least one front-end framework (React, Vue.js, or Angular)
  • Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP)
  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills — you can earn trust quickly, navigate ambiguity, and drive alignment across diverse teams
  • Comfort operating in fast-paced environments with shifting priorities, high ownership expectations, and occasional on-call responsibility
  • Experience mentoring or supporting junior engineers in their technical development
Desirable Skills
  • Experience with RAG architectures, vector databases (Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector), and semantic search
  • Familiarity with prompt engineering, fine-tuning, and LLM evaluation techniques
  • Experience with agent observability and tracing tools (LangSmith, Arize, Weights & Biases, or similar)
  • Strong UX instincts — ability to simplify complex flows and make agent outputs accessible and actionable for non-technical stakeholders
  • Experience with containerization and CI/CD practices (Docker, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions)
  • Background in real estate, financial services, or other data-intensive enterprise domains
  • Experience facilitating technical discovery workshops, design sprints, or architecture reviews
