title: Product Designer, Marketing & GTM
location: New York, NY or Los Angeles, CA
description:
The Opportunity

We're hiring a mid-level Product Designer to be the creative partner behind Enigma's go-to-market efforts. Our identity is mid-refresh, so this isn't a role that only applies to our existing design system, you'll help systematize its evolution. You'll work directly with our marketing lead (a generalist across channels and strategy) to turn GTM ideas into campaigns, web pages, sales collateral, and social content.

What You’ll Do

  • Shape GTM creative, don't just execute it. Partner on campaign concepts and go-to-market ideas, bringing your own point of view rather than filling in a pre-set brief.
  • Systematize the brand system. Contribute to Enigma's brand organization including but not limited to maintaining asset libraries, deck templates, and brand guideline documents.
  • Build and update the website. Design and ship pages directly in our custom CMS (deployed on Vercel), from layout to content to launch, alongside marketing and engineering.
  • Create sales and marketing collateral. One-pagers, case studies, pitch decks, and flexible slide systems the team can reuse for sales, marketing, and leadership.
  • Own social and campaign content. Design LinkedIn carousels and campaign graphics, and cut short-form video (“cut-ups”) from longer source material.
  • Design HubSpot campaign assets. Email templates and campaign landing pages that support lifecycle and demand-gen marketing.
  • Prep imagery. Retouch and prepare hero and content images for web, social, and marketing channels.
  • Use AI as part of the workflow. Use Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini etc. for ideation, copy support, team collaboration, and speeding up production, we want someone comfortable working this way, not resistant to it.
  • Maintain consistency. Typography, color, imagery, and tone stay on-brand across every deliverable.

What Makes This Role Exciting?

  • Real ownership: you're helping build the brand system, not just maintaining one that's already locked.
  • A true creative partnership: you'll work directly with a marketing generalist founder who needs a creative mind to round out GTM strategy, not just a pair of hands.
  • Variety and speed: brand, web, video, decks, email, and social, your work ships into real campaigns fast, with visible results that contribute to overall KPIs

Our Ideal Candidate

  • 3–5 years as a designer supporting marketing, GTM, or brand teams either in-house at a startup or in an agency setting.
  • A creative point of view, not just production skill. Comfortable proposing ideas and pushing back on a brief, not only fulfilling it.
  • Comfort building within a brand system while it's still in motion — our guidelines are actively developing, not fixed. You will be bringing structure: organizing, documenting, and systematizing as it takes shape.
  • Proficiency in Figma and Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere).
  • Experience designing HubSpot campaign assets (email, landing pages).
  • Comfortable building and editing pages in a custom CMS; familiarity with Vercel-hosted sites is a plus.
  • Skilled at building slide systems/templates in Figma, Keynote, or PowerPoint/Google Slides that others can use and extend.
  • Comfortable editing short-form video (cut-downs, captions, simple motion/text treatments) using Premiere, CapCut, or After Effects.
  • Familiarity with using Claude or similar AI tools as part of a creative workflow.
  • Experience designing for a B2B, data, fintech, or enterprise brand is a plus.
  • Self-directed, responsive, and comfortable with quick-turnaround requests and shifting priorities.
  • Based in New York, NY or Los Angeles, CA and able to work in-office. This is an in-person role — being on-site is how we move fast and stay closely aligned.

Bonus Points If You

  • Have led or significantly contributed to a brand system/rebrand at a growing company.
  • Have basic motion graphics or animation skills.
  • Have experience making complex data feel simple and visual, relevant to Enigma's data-driven product.
  • Have written or edited marketing copy alongside design work.

About Us

At Enigma, we’re building the single, most reliable source of data on businesses to power the future of financial services. By engineering better data from hundreds of public and third-party sources, we aim to tell the complete story of every business, so that companies of every size can access the financial services they need to grow and thrive.

Our core values – generosity, curiosity, ingenuity, & drive – guide everything we do, from how we make our most important product decisions to how we work with and support one another on a daily basis. We’re a team of curious, driven individuals with diverse backgrounds and skills, but we’re all passionate about engineering deeper understanding through data—together. If this resonates, we would love to hear from you!

title: Class A Driver
description:

MedTrans is Medline's private fleet of professional drivers that delivers our lifesaving medical products directly to both commercial and residential customers. Our fleet consists of 2,100+ trucks that feature newer equipment. We manage a network of over 50 distribution centers nationally and provide 1-day shipping to 95% of the United States.

The Driver is responsible for operating a Class A vehicle to transport life-saving medical products to our local customers. The Driver plays a critical role in building positive relationships with our customers by ensuring timely, accurate, and safe deliveries.

title: Konsulent til strategisk udvikling af forebyggelse og sundhedsfremme
description:
Er du skarp til at koble politiske processer med implementeringstiltag, der kan mærkes helt ude i fingerspidserne af organisationen? Og brænder du for at arbejde i spændingsfeltet mellem sundhed og politik?

I så fald er du måske vores nye konsulent til Staben for Ældre, Sundhed og Social. Regeringen indgik tilbage i november 2024 en bred politisk aftale om en sundhedsreform, som har til formål at styrke sundhedsvæsnet og rykke det tættere på borgerne. Aftalen indeholder mange elementer, heriblandt en nytænkning af den sundhedsfremmende og forebyggende indsats i kommunerne. Vi søger nu en konsulent, som kan samle trådene i arbejdet med at implementere Sundhedsreformen samtidig med en udvikling af kommunens sundhedsfremmende og forebyggende indsats.

Albertslund er en grøn kommune med store ambitioner. Vi er stolte af vores kommune, og gør os umage i vores opgaver og indsatser for borgerne, foreningerne og virksomhederne. Vi er én kommune og én organisation. Vi har engagerede og dygtige medarbejdere samt en samarbejdskultur, der går på tværs af områder og niveauer. Det gør Albertslund Kommune til et godt sted at arbejde.

Om opgaverne

Dine opgaver vil helt overordnet være fordelt på et strategisk udviklingsarbejde i forhold til sundhedsfremme og forebyggelse og en tovholderfunktion på de elementer, Sundhedsreformen kalder på, at vi som kommune forholder os til.

Som vores nye sundhedskonsulent, vil du få en vigtig rolle i at drive og udvikle på de eksisterende sundhedsrelaterede projekter og sikre strategisk retning i samarbejde med ledelsen. Af konkrete projekter kan nævnes Klar Livet, udvikling af rådgivningstilbud om rusmidler til unge og udvikling af kommunens rygestoptilbud. Det er derfor vigtigt, at du har en god organisationsforståelse og samtidig har en faglighed at trække på i forhold til at kunne arbejde med udvikling af sundhedsfremme og forebyggelse. Der vil også være opgaver, som omfatter sagsfremstillinger til politisk niveau og andre typer udviklingsarbejde.

Staben for Ældre, Sundhed og Social fungerer som bindeled mellem kommunens ledelse, samarbejdspartnere og afdelingens borgerrettede tilbud, og du skal derfor kunne indgå i opgaver, som spænder bredt. Staben består for nuværende af 17 dygtige medarbejdere med forskellige fagligheder, som spiller ind i disse dagsordener.

I Albertslund Kommune kommer vi de kommende år til at arbejde målrettet på at skabe sammenhæng og synergi på tværs af sundheds-, ældre- og socialområdet, der også har samme chef. Staben understøtter alle tre områder, og vi anser det som en positiv værdi, at vi samarbejder på tværs. Derfor vil det være en del af opgaven, at vi ikke ser udviklingen i det nære sundhedsvæsen snævert, men hele tiden tænker alle tre områder ind, hvor det måtte være relevant, ligesom vi har en opgave i at tænke sundhed som et område hvor vi skal skabe et endnu stærkere samarbejde med vores kolleger på kommunens andre fagområder.

Dine kompetencer

Vi søger en kollega, der har erfaring fra lignende stillinger, og som har et fagligt fundament på kandidatniveau for at indgå i opgaverne. Du kan være uddannet i folkesundhedsvidenskab, men andre samfundsvidenskabelige uddannelser vil også være relevante eksempelvis statskundskab, politik og administration og lignende.

Derudover ser vi på, om du:

  • har erfaring med politisk betjening og en god organisationsforståelse
  • kan drive processer og skabe ejerskab hos de medvirkende
  • kan navigere smidigt i et felt med mange forskelligartede interesser
  • er dygtig til at skabe solide samarbejdsrelationer
  • er ansvarsfuld og drivende på egne opgaver
  • har en skarp pen og er en dygtig mundtlig formidler

Det er vigtigt for os, at du kan tænke strategisk. Erfaring fra sundheds- og ældreområdet vil være en fordel, men ikke et krav.

Vi kan tilbyde

Du vil blive en del af en afdeling, som har en opgaveportefølje i stor udvikling, og som spænder meget bredt. Vi kan derfor tilbyde et miljø, hvor udvikling er i højsædet, og hvor vi tager fælles ansvar for at spille hinanden og afdelingen god. Vi mener, det skal være sjovt og spændende at gå på arbejde, fordi vi tror på, at det er forudsætningen for, at vi løser vores opgaver bedst muligt. Derfor kan vi også tilbyde et job, hvor der er rig mulighed for faglig og personlig udvikling, og hvor relationen til kollegerne prioriteres højt.

Om os

Staben for Sundhed, Ældre og Social er en enhed, som vægter det sociale højt, fordi vi tror på, at det er vigtigt at have det godt sammen, når vi går på arbejde. Det er både godt for os selv og for opgaveløsningen. Vi arbejder i en teamstruktur, hvor man refererer til afdelingsleder, Julie Teresa Neidhardt, og du vil blive en del af vores konsulentteam, hvor vi lægger vægt på at have et fagligt miljø med et højt ambitionsniveau og en uformel omgangstone.

Det praktiske

Løn og ansættelse sker efter gældende overenskomst, og arbejdstiden er 37 timer.

Ansøgningsfristen er den 20. august kl. 8, og der afholdes samtaler den 26. august.

Forventet opstart 1. oktober 2026 eller før.

Hvis du har spørgsmål eller er blevet nysgerrig på at høre mere om jobbet, er du velkommen til at kontakte stabsleder Julie Teresa Neidhardt på telefon 20 21 64 47.

Arbejdsstedet er Normarks Allé 1, 2620 Albertslund.

Lønindplacering sker efter forhandling mellem kommunen og den forhandlingsberettigede organisation.

Det er en del af Albertslund Kommunes ansættelsespolitik at fremme mangfoldighed og ligestilling.

Det er en forudsætning for din ansættelse i Albertslund Kommune, at du har en gyldig arbejds- og opholdstilladelse.

Albertslund Kommune har røgfri arbejdstid.

"Om Albertslund Kommune"

Velkommen til Albertslund - den bæredygtige by for børnene, det grønne og fællesskaber. Albertslund Kommune har mange kvaliteter, som skaber fantastiske rammer for hverdagslivet – både for borgere og medarbejdere. Midt i naturen og med et rigt forenings- og kulturliv, som børn og voksne cykler til og fra på byens mange kilometer cykelstier, der er adskilt fra bilerne på vejene. Der er S-tog lige til døren og flere supercykelstier, bl.a. mellem Albertslund og Vesterport i hjertet af København. Desuden skaber letbanen gode forbindelser til hele hovedstadsområdet.

I Albertslund Kommune har vi samme tilgang til vores opgaver, som vi selv ville ønske at opleve som borgere. Vi er vidt forskellige, men er fælles om vores opgave for borgere, foreninger og virksomheder. Du kan møde nogle af vores dygtige medarbejdere på www.albertslund.dk/indefra og få et indtryk af bredden af arbejdsområder, opgaver og fagligheder i Albertslund Kommune.

I Albertslund Kommune er der højt til loftet og gode udviklingsmuligheder - vi glæder os til at høre fra dig.

Summary of Job Duties:

POSITION SUMMARY

The Winthrop P. Rockefeller Cancer Institute (WPRCI) at the University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences (UAMS) in Little Rock is seeking a manager for a newly founded Cryo-EM Facility. This facility will be equipped with a 200kV Glacios TEM, Falcon 4i direct electron detector, Selectris X Energy Filter, and auxiliary instrumentation for single particle sample preparation including vitrification devices (e.g., Vitrobot and Leica GP2). The successful candidate will be responsible for daily operations, cryo-EM sample vitrification, data collection and on-the-fly processing, and interaction with and training of users. Users will be from UAMS and institutions in Arkansas and the surrounding states.

The University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences (UAMS) has a unique combination of education, research, and clinical programs that encourages and supports teamwork and diversity. We champion being a collaborative health care organization, focused on improving patient care and the lives of Arkansans.

All UAMS employees will treat others with Dignity and Respect. We communicate and share complete and unbiased information, assuring our colleagues receive timely, complete, and accurate information in order to make informed decisions.
We participate in institutional initiatives and encourage the participation of others. We collaborate in policy and program development, implementation, and evaluation using best practices in delivering quality service. All duties will be performed in accordance with the UAMS Core Concepts of Patient and Family Centered Care set forth by UAMS. These core concepts allow for an approach to health care that shapes policies, programs, facility design and staff day-to-day interactions. It leads to better health outcomes and wiser allocation of resources, and greater patient and family satisfaction. The core concepts of patient and family centered care consist of Dignity & Respect, Information Sharing, Participation, and Collaboration.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Four (4+) years (Associate Scientist) or

  • Seven (7+) years (Principal Scientist) of relevant experience including significant project management experience, personnel supervision and editorial and scientific contributions to grants.

  • Record of expertise in cryo-EM-based structural biology research founded on publications

  • Technical skills in cryo-EM sample vitrification, data acquisition, data processing and data analysis

• Experience with routine maintenance of accessory equipment
• Expertise with data collection and processing software for single particle analysis, including Cryosparc and Relion

• Keep accurate and clear records to help writing of manuscripts and center-related grant proposals as needed
• Keep up with scientific literature relevant to new instrumentation, data processing, specimen preparation and imaging techniques.

Lige nu søger vi 1 jobkonsulent i Borger, Arbejdsmarked & Erhverv i team Tidlig Indsats, til at arbejde med sygedagpengemodtagere med ledighed fra 0–26 uger. I teamet arbejdes der også med dagpengemodtagere, modtagere af ledighedsydelse samt jobparate kontanthjælpsmodtagere med ledighed 0-26/52 ugers ledighed.

Om opgaven
Du kommer til at arbejde i en organisation, hvor vi arbejder på tværs af alle teams i Jobcenteret samt har en tæt kontakt til medarbejderne i ydelsescentret, så vi sammen kan yde en kvalificeret og sammenhængende indsats for borgerne.

Vi leder efter dig, der helt naturligt arbejder job- og virksomhedsrettet og vil være med til at gøre en reel forskel og give endnu flere borgere mulighed for at opnå eller fastholde tilknytning til arbejdsmarkedet. Også dem, der har sproglige barrierer eller andre udfordringer.

Du skal have lyst til at bidrage til den udvikling, vores organisation står i. Det indebærer, at det falder dig naturligt at komme med faglige input og forslag til løbende optimering af opgaveløsningen, og at vi løbende foretager justeringer i vores måde at arbejde på for at opnå større effekt af vores indsats.

  • Formidling til praktik, løntilskud og ordinært arbejde
  • Selvstændig kontakt til virksomheder for at skabe muligheder for praktik, delvis tilbagevenden eller job
  • Selvstændig sagsbehandling
  • Koordinering af planer og progression med henblik på tilbagevenden til arbejde
  • Myndighedsopgaver, herunder opfølgning, koordinering og dokumentation i henhold til gældende lovgivning
  • Samarbejde med interne og eksterne aktører, herunder læger, behandlere og virksomheder
  • Motiverende og afklarende samtaler med borgerne


I stillingen forventer vi, at du:

  • Har erfaring med at skabe progression mod job for ledige borgere
  • Har erfaring med at anvende virksomhedspraktik og løntilskud som redskab til ordinær beskæftigelse
  • Trives med selvstændigt at kontakte virksomheder for at skabe muligheder for job og praktik/løntilskud
  • Arbejder struktureret og har stærke dokumentationsevner
  • Har erfaring med beskæftigelsesområdet og kan navigere i LAB-lovgivningen
  • Er fleksibel og har gode samarbejdsevner
  • Har lyst til at arbejde målrettet og ressourceorienteret med borgerne og ser sproglige barrierer som en faglig udfordring – ikke en forhindring.

title: Engineering Services Specialist
description:
About Carrier

Carrier Global Corporation, global leader in intelligent climate and energy solutions, is committed to creating innovations that bring comfort, safety and sustainability to life. Through cutting-edge advancements in climate solutions such as temperature control, air quality and transportation, we improve lives, empower critical industries and ensure the safe transport of food, life-saving medicines and more. Since inventing modern air conditioning in 1902, we lead with purpose: enhancing the lives we live and the world we share. We continue to lead because of our world-class, inclusive workforce that puts the customer at the center of everything we do. For more information, visit corporate.carrier.com or follow Carrier on social media at @Carrier.

About the Role

The Engineering Services Specialist supports Carrier Design Engineering teams across Mexico and the United States by facilitating engineering changes and maintaining product documentation within the Windchill Product Data Management (PDM) system. In this role, you will ensure the accuracy of Bills of Materials (BOMs), engineering drawings, specifications, and product records while enabling efficient engineering change management processes that support business and customer needs.

Key Responsibilities

As an Engineering Services Specialist, you'll be responsible for:

  • Creating and processing engineering change documentation within the Windchill PDM system.

  • Updating and maintaining Bills of Materials (BOMs), engineering drawings, specifications, and related product documentation.

  • Interpreting engineering markups, technical instructions, customer requirements, and change requests to accurately implement design changes.

  • Managing part creation, revision control, drawing modifications, and BOM updates throughout the product lifecycle.

  • Determining implementation plans for change requests and routing tasks to appropriate stakeholders through Windchill workflows.

  • Communicating regularly with engineering teams and key stakeholders regarding open actions, document status, and change implementation progress.

  • Monitoring engineering change metrics and supporting continuous improvement initiatives.

  • Maintaining team databases, records, and reporting metrics.

  • Creating Approved Vendor Lists (AVL) and drawings for control box components and control boards.

  • Supporting special projects and process improvement initiatives that enhance team effectiveness and operational efficiency.

Requirements

We are looking for people who are highly organized, detail-oriented, analytical, collaborative, and customer-focused. If this sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you.

As a minimum you must have:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical field.

  • Minimum 5 years of experience supporting engineering documentation, engineering change management, product data management (PDM), or related engineering processes.

  • Experience working with engineering documentation, Bills of Materials (BOMs), engineering drawings, and configuration management processes.

  • Understanding of engineering documentation and engineering change management processes.

  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining a high level of accuracy and attention to detail.

  • Ability to communicate professionally in both written and verbal formats across a diverse audience.

  • Advanced English communication skills.

Although not necessary, it would be nice if you have:

  • Experience with Windchill PDM.

  • Experience creating or modifying engineering drawings using CAD or similar software.

  • Knowledge of AVL management and product lifecycle management processes.

Benefits

We offer a competitive total rewards package that may include other benefits and well-being programs. Offerings vary by role and location and are designed to support employees’ health, security, and success.

This hands-on position combines platform engineering, cloud infrastructure, and software development to create scalable self-service capabilities that accelerate innovation. Working in a remote-first and highly collaborative environment, you will partner with engineering and research teams to build reliable, secure, and reusable platform services. title: Executive Protection Agent
description:
Voyager is an innovative space, defense, and national security technology company committed to advancing and delivering transformative, mission-critical solutions. We tackle the most complex challenges to unlock new frontiers for human progress, fortify national security, and protect critical assets to lead in the race for technological and operational superiority from ground to space.

Forge the Future: Join Voyager Technologies

The future belongs to those who build it. At Voyager Technologies, we’re building technologies that protect lives, expand frontiers and prepare us for what’s next. And we’re doing that with people who are wired to solve, build, adapt and lead. These roles are not for the faint of heart.

You’ll help lay the foundation for humanity's future. Join a culture where innovation thrives, curiosity is rewarded, and impact is real. We’re a company of doers, thinkers and builders, united by purpose and grounded in reality.

If you want to put your skills to work where the stakes are real and the mission is bigger than any one person, forge the future with Voyager.

Voyager Technologies is seeking an experienced Executive Protection Agent to provide dedicated, low-profile protection for its Chairman & CEO. The Agent will be solely accountable for the full spectrum of protective operations — from meticulous advance planning to real-time decision-making — across daily movements, domestic and international travel, and high-profile engagements. This role demands seamless integration into executive environments. The principal's program prioritizes advance work, operational discretion, and low-profile bearing. Candidates must be prepared to operate in business attire, lead with judgment and tradecraft, and protect without disrupting the pace or profile of a senior executive at the highest levels of corporate life. Candidates should expect to spend the majority of working time in the field — in transit with the principal, or supporting advance and event coverage. This is not a desk role.

Duties & Responsibilities

● Provide direct, armed close protection of the principal across workplace, mobile, and travel-based environments.
● Plan, conduct, and own all advance work for movements, venues, and events.
● Maintain continuous situational awareness; proactively identify, assess, and mitigate risks to the principal in real time.
● Make immediate, independent operational decisions to ensure principal safety and mobility — including adjusting routes, protective posture, and contingency actions as conditions require.
● Execute seamless mobility without disrupting the principal's business operations or public profile.
● Coordinate and manage transportation, logistics, and movement execution, including vehicles, drivers, and third-party resources.
● Support protective operations for associated principals as directed, maintaining identical standards of discretion and performance.
● Match the principal's style and pace while sustaining full protective effectiveness at all times.
● Render emergency medical care if required.
● Integrate effectively with internal stakeholders and external partners to ensure coordinated, frictionless protective operations.
● Maintain continuous communication with the operational lead, ensuring full visibility into plans, movements, and emerging risks.
● Document operational activity, incidents, and observations; contribute meaningfully to after-action reviews and continuous improvement.

If your experience aligns with our basic qualifications and you are inspired by our mission, we’d like to connect. If you don’t see the right role right now, Join Our Talent Community and stay connected as we continue to build what’s next.

Minimum Qualifications
Do not apply without meeting all of the following requirements.

● 10+ years of active, field-based protective security experience with direct responsibility for safety and security operations. Qualifying experience must be derived from military, law enforcement, federal protective services, or equivalent private-sector roles. No credit given for administrative, support, or non-operational assignments.
● Demonstrated executive protection experience in a corporate environment (in-house or contract-supporting corporate), including close protection, advance work, and movement operations.
● At least some prior U.S. military background.
● Current CPR / AED / First Aid certification.
● Established working relationships with law enforcement and corporate security counterparts.
● Completion of a formal Executive Protection training program and/or recognized industry EP certifications.
● Strong judgment, professionalism, and discretion in dynamic and sensitive situations.
● Valid U.S. Passport with availability for domestic and international travel.
● Willingness to travel extensively (approximately 60–75%) and provide 24/7 availability as the role demands.
● Professional bearing and presentation appropriate for C-suite, boardroom, and high-visibility public environments.
● Physical fitness consistent with military or military contracting standards; clean, professional appearance.
● Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams).
● Clean criminal background, valid driver's license, and clean driving record.

Preferred Qualifications:
Meeting any of the following will increase your competitiveness in the selection process.

● Prior U.S. military SOF background; AFSOC pipelines (CCT, PJ, TACP, SR) and Green Beret, Navy SEAL, Army Ranger are particularly valued.
● Completion of a recognized protective driving or advanced vehicle dynamics program.
● Experience supporting principals with significant public profile or media exposure.
● Familiarity with executive aviation logistics, FBO transitions, and corporate transportation coordination.
● Professional certifications: EP, CPP, PSP, or equivalent credentials.

This position requires the highest standards of discretion, integrity, and professional commitment. Only those who meet all minimum qualifications and are prepared for a demanding, field-forward role need apply.

This position is incentive/bonus plan eligible.

The good-faith base salary range for this role is $150,000 - $160,000 at the time of this posting. Where you fall within the range depends on your experience, skills, and location. This range reflects base salary only and does not include benefits or bonus/incentive. This range may be adjusted in the future.

Voyager offers a highly competitive total compensation package designed to support the well-being, growth, and success of our employees. Employees benefit from a flexible and comprehensive rewards program that supports both professional and personal well-being.

  • Flexible Time Off (FTO), empowering employees to take the time they need to recharge and maintain a healthy work-life balance
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and their families, with a significant portion of premiums covered by the company and many benefits paid at 100% for employees
  • Flexible, affordable gym memberships with 12,700+ options nationwide, including 24 Hour Fitness, EoS Fitness, Crunch Fitness, Anytime Fitness, Blink Fitness, Chuze Fitness, and more! No long-term contracts and FREE on-demand workout videos before you enroll
  • 401(k) retirement plan with a 50% company match on contributions up to 8%, supporting long-term financial security
  • Company wellness programs that support physical and mental well-being
  • Additional voluntary benefits and employee support resources
  • The opportunity to work alongside a highly talented team in an innovative, mission-driven environment

Voyager is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status, or other characteristics protected by law.

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) (22 CFR Parts 120–130) and the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) (15 CFR Parts 730–774), applicants for this position must be a U.S. Person: a US Citizen, a lawful permanent resident of the U.S., or a protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. § 1324b(a)(3). title: Associate Medical Safety Director
description:
Job Overview
Provide medical expertise on pharmacovigilance services to divisions as requested. The Associate Medical Safety Director participates in all aspects of Medical Safety’s involvement on assigned trials and stand alone safety projects with appropriate oversight from management or more senior medical safety directors.

Essential Functions
• Perform medical review and clarification of trial-related Adverse Events (AEs) and post-marketing adverse drug reactions (ADRs) including narrative content, queries, coding, expectedness, seriousness, causality and company summary
• Compose, edit and medically review Analyses of Similar Events (AOSE) for expedited cases as appropriate based on regulatory requirements
• Serve as an internal consultant to pharmacovigilance case processing teams on projects being supported
• Provide aggregate reviews of safety information, including clinical data, to maintain oversight of a product’s safety profile
• Provide coding review of AEs, Past medical history, Concomitant medications or other medical data listings to verify and medically vet clinical data
• Represent safety and clinical data review findings during client meetings
• Provide medical review and edits to IND Annual Reports, EU Periodic Benefit Risk Evaluation Reports, EU Periodic Safety Update Reports, EU Development Safety Update Reports, US Periodic Reports
• Provide medical review and edits of Development Risk Management Plans, EU Risk Management Plans or US Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies
• Provide medical oversight for label development, review and change
• Provide medical support and attendance at Data Safety Monitoring Board Meetings
• Attends and contributes medical safety evaluation on Safety Monitoring Committees
• Provide medical safety contributions to the Integrated Safety Summary or Common Technical Document
• Provide medical review and edits to Drug Safety Reports or other benefit-risk assessments
• Review and sign off on both the Project Safety Plan and the Medical Monitoring Plan per medical safety scope agreed in contract
• Perform Medical Safety review of the protocol, Investigative Drug Brochure (IDB), and/or Case Report Forms (CRFs) for appropriate safety content and data capture.
• Act as Global Safety Physician or Assistant or Back-up on projects as assigned
• Attend project meetings, medical safety team meetings, and client meetings as requested
• Ensure coverage for all medical safety deliverables within regulatory or contracted timelines
• Provide medical escalation support for medical information projects
• Provide medical escalation support for EU Qualified Persons for Pharmacovigilance projects
• 24 hour medical support as required on assigned projects
• Maintain awareness of medical-safety-regulatory industry developments

Qualifications
• Medical degree from an accredited and internationally recognized medical school (Bachelor's Degree in Medicine necessary).
• 7+ years of clinical practice experience: Signal management activities, review clinical trial documents, creation, analysis, and presentation of reports (aggregate reports), client facing activities, risk management.

• 9+ additional years in the pharmaceutical or associated industry.
• Knowledge of applicable federal and local regulations and guidelines pertaining to clinical research including knowledge of regulations and guidelines pertaining to safety and good clinical practice
• Knowledge of clinical trials and pharmaceutical research process
• Ability to establish and meet priorities, deadlines, and objectives.
• Skills in providing consultation and advice on multiple assignments required, as well as initiative and flexibility
• Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with coworkers, managers and clients
• A valid medical license, or equivalent, from the country or region in which he/she resides and works

title: Requirements Evaluation and Design (RED) Team Lead
description:
Competitive Range partners with the government to plan and deploy complex, IT-enabled, and mission-essential capabilities. Our goal is to help you develop and expand your professional capabilities while working on challenging, exciting projects in a collaborative, congenial environment.

Competitive Range Solutions requires the expertise of a talented and experienced Requirements Evaluation and Design (RED) Team leader to assist in directing and managing the program’s executive support group. The candidate must reference their ability and experience working in a Department of Defense (DoD) customer environment and effective integration with a government multi-contractor team.

The RED Team Lead is key in focusing on the critical assessment and design phases of Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs) for IT infrastructure and network architecture enhancement. This position involves leading a team that evaluates network requirements, develops technical solutions, and ensures the design meets customer needs and government standards without increasing costs. The RED Team Lead will work closely with DOD customers and other stakeholders to navigate the complexities of system upgrades, network modernization, technology refreshment projects, and more.

Roles and Responsibilities:

  • Lead the team in assessing customer-submitted network requirements through a government-provided service ticketing application.
  • Guide the team in providing necessary support to DoD customers for the articulation of their network needs.
  • Direct the design process for ECPs, ensuring that proposed IT infrastructure and network architecture changes are robust, cost-effective, and compliant with existing standards.
  • Manage the development of technical solutions that align with project types defined in the ECP Catalog.
  • Act as the primary liaison between the project team and DoD customers to clarify requirements, discuss technical solutions, and address negative project execution challenges.
  • Ensure regular customer communication, especially regarding hardware-based requirements and delivery timelines.
  • Oversee the creation of project documentation, including Change Requests, ECP Waiver Requests, and Status Reports.
  • Implement project management best practices within the team to meet deliverables’ timelines and quality standards.
  • Identify opportunities for process improvements and innovative solutions to meet complex project requirements. Foster a culture of continuous learning and adaptation within the team.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously with a meticulous approach and under tight deadlines.

Qualifications/Experience:

  • Active TS/SCI Clearance
  • 5+ years as Lead Project Manager
  • 5+ years in DoD IT environment
  • Outstanding mathematics and IT abilities
  • Proficient in preparing detailed cost estimate reports.
  • Proficient in relevant software tools, including MS Office
  • Proven self-management and team-management skills.
  • Must possess expert managerial, leadership, and communication skills.

Education/Certifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in information systems, computer sciences, business management, or related field (Required)
  • Master's degree (Preferred)
  • PMP (Minimum)

title: Adjunct Instructor of Instrumentation Controls and Electrical Technology Program
description:
Compensation:

$30.64 - $45.26 per hour

Up to 29 hours per week

Non-Exempt

Adjunct/Part Time Faculty (Fixed Term)

Grade:

NE15

Position Summary

The position will report to the Instrumentation Program Coordinator and will be responsible for classroom and lab instruction of students in the Instrumentation Controls & Electrical Technology Program.

San Juan College may approve remote or hybrid work for adjunct employees within New Mexico, Arizona, Colorado and Texas (states subject to change at any time). All requests for remote work must be approved in advance by the Dean and Human Resources. Remote work options for locations outside of the United States are not permitted.

MAJOR DUTIES

  • The instructor will work well in a team environment, sharing responsibilities with other members of the department for program and curriculum development, maintaining a record system for student achievement, and delivering/creating customized training for industry.

  • Designs learning experiences such as projects and reflections, problem sets and quizzes

  • Uses College Learning Management System (Canvas) for course delivery, attendance, participation and grades.

  • Maintains labs and equipment

KNOWLEDGE REQUIRED BY THE POSITION

  • Knowledge of safety protocols, process safety, PPE, and safe work practices

  • Ability to perform, troubleshoot, and teach hands-on labs.
  • Understanding of electrical theories including Ohm’s Law, Power Law, and electrical circuit analysis.

  • Knowledge of electrical components and both AC/DC systems.

  • Knowledge of electrical codes and standards.

  • Knowledge in electrical motor and motor control.

  • Skills in using instruments such as multimeters, clamp meters, oscilloscopes, etc.

  • Skills in industrial electrical tasks such as conduit bending, wiring, and installation of electrical devices.

  • Skill in the operation of computers and job-related software programs.

  • Skill in decision making and problem solving.

  • Skill in interpersonal relations and in dealing with the public.

  • Skill in working effectively with a wide range of constituencies in a diverse community.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

  • Knowledge and level of competency commonly associated with the completion of a bachelor’s degree in the field or a combination of education, training and tested experience sufficient to thoroughly understand the objectives and functions of the discipline they teach.

  • Possession of or ability to readily obtain a valid driver’s license issued by the State of New Mexico for the type of vehicle or equipment operated.

  • Must be able to pass a background check.

Adjunct faculty are hired on a semester basis, depending upon the instructional needs identified for each semester. Such services shall be compensated on a credit hour or contact hour basis, dependent upon the position.

It is the policy of San Juan College that adjunct faculty may teach no more than 9 credit hours per semester, except upon approval by the Vice-President of Learning and the Vice-President of HR and Legal Activities.

Payroll and Benefits:

Adjunct faculty are paid bi-weekly. Adjunct faculty are paid at either $801 per credit hour, or at an hourly rate as applicable.

Adjunct faculty teaching one (1) credit class or more are eligible for the tuition waiver benefit. Tuition may be waived for one class, up to four (4) credit hours per semester, and any one (1) credit HHPC Fitness Conditioning class for each semester they are employed. This tuition waiver benefit may be transferred to a qualified family member for the semester they are employed. • Free Library Services (CD and DVD checkout; book and periodical checkout).

• Voluntary Benefits

o Allstate/Aflac

o Liberty Mutual

Adjunct faculty teaching three (3) or more credit hours will have Educational Retirement Board (ERB) contributions withheld each pay period. Contribution rates and retirement eligibility are available on the State of New Mexico Educational Retirement Board website http://www.nmerb.org Adjunct faculty are not medical benefit eligible. State and federal taxes, FICA and social security will be withheld for all adjunct faculty. Unofficial transcripts may be attached to this application.

Official transcripts must be sent to Human Resources upon hire.

title: LAI Senior Director - Administration - Operations & Strategy
location: Philadelphia Campus- Roberts Center for Pediatric Research
description:
SHIFT:

Day (United States of America)

Seeking Breakthrough Makers

Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) offers countless ways to change lives. Our diverse community of more than 20,000 Breakthrough Makers will inspire you to pursue passions, develop expertise, and drive innovation.

At CHOP, your experience is valued; your voice is heard; and your contributions make a difference for patients and families. Join us as we build on our promise to advance pediatric care—and your career.

CHOP does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, sex, national origin, religion, or any other legally protected categories in any employment, training, or vendor decisions or programs. CHOP recognizes the critical importance of a workforce rich in varied backgrounds and experiences and engages in ongoing efforts to achieve that through equally varied and non-discriminatory means.


A Brief Overview


The Lurie Autism Institute is a groundbreaking research institute jointly established by the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) and the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania (Penn Medicine), founded through a transformative gift from the Lurie Family Foundation and the Nancy Lurie Marks Family Foundation. Designed as a preeminent international center for autism research, the Institute unites CHOP's renowned pediatric research enterprise with Penn Medicine's world-class medical and scientific community to accelerate discovery, collaboration, and real-world impact in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The Senior Director, Administration, Operations & Strategy serves as the senior operational leader of the Lurie Autism Institute, working in close partnership with the Founding Scientific Director to translate the Institute's visionary goals into sustainable, high-performing operations. As senior administrative, operational, and strategy officer, the Senior Director is responsible for building and maintaining the infrastructure, staffing, financial systems, and strategic communications frameworks that support the Institute's mission and ensure all scientific and programmatic efforts are grounded in sound, scalable operations. This role offers a unique opportunity to shape and steward a newly launched, high-profile, bi-institutional research institute. The Senior Director will operate at the intersection of science, strategy, philanthropy, and institutional partnership to position the Lurie Autism Institute as a global leader in autism research and innovation. The ideal candidate is a strategic, results-oriented administrative executive with proven leadership experience in complex, matrixed organizations, within academic medicine, research institutes, major non-profits, or industry. They are a systems thinker and skilled relationship-builder who thrives in innovative environments, bringing both operational rigor and creative problem-solving.

What you will do

Strategic Leadership & Partnership

  • Serve as the chief administrative partner to the Scientific Director, co-leading strategic planning, institutional growth, and mission execution.
  • Translate mid- and long-term vision into actionable plans, scalable processes, and staffing models.
  • Represent the Institute to internal and external stakeholders, including CHOP and Penn development teams, donors, and advisory groups, alongside or on behalf of the Scientific Director.
  • Ensure Institute operations remain agile and responsive to evolving scientific priorities, philanthropic strategies, and institutional opportunities.
  • Partner with scientific and academic leaders in collaborative governance models.

Operational & Administrative Management

  • Build and oversee all core administrative functions: finance, HR coordination, facilities, compliance, IT, procurement, and research operations, including collaboration with CHOP and Penn leadership.
  • Establish joint operating protocols and collaborative systems that align with the policies and cultures of both CHOP and Penn.
  • Ensure compliance with all relevant institutional, sponsor, and donor requirements, including those specified in formal gift agreements.

Financial Stewardship

  • Lead all aspects of financial strategy, including annual budget development in partnership with the Scientific Director and CHOP and Penn Chief Scientific Officers.
  • Oversee financial management of the Lurie Autism Institute Term Fund and Research and Program Endowed Fund, ensuring adherence to donor intent and institutional policies in collaboration with CHOP and Penn finance partners.
  • Monitor and report on Institute expenditures and revenues, including indirect costs, maintaining alignment with CHOP and Penn financial governance standards.
  • Support philanthropic stewardship efforts alongside CHOP and Penn development teams, including preparation of annual joint donor reports.
  • Collaborate with the Scientific Director and other stakeholders to prepare and co-lead biannual stewardship meetings.

Marketing & Public Relations

  • Lead development of a cohesive, mission-driven messaging and branding strategy for the Lurie Autism Institute in partnership with CHOP and Penn marketing and communications teams, ensuring unified positioning across channels.
  • Collaborate with the Scientific Director to implement communications plans that elevate the Institute’s visibility, impact, and reputation as a leader in autism research.
  • Oversee creation and dissemination of high-impact materials and digital content highlighting scientific milestones, strategic initiatives, and community engagement.
  • Support planning and promotion of key events, conferences, and donor communications to strengthen public awareness and stakeholder engagement.

Institutional Relations & Governance

  • Serve as a primary liaison to administrative leaders and offices at both CHOP and Penn.
  • Coordinate the Institute’s engagement with the Internal (CHOP/Penn) Lurie Institute Advisory Committee, the Scientific Advisory Board, and the Community Advisory Board, including meeting planning, materials preparation, and follow-up actions.
  • Support execution of responsibilities outlined in the CHOP and Penn gift agreements, including donor recognition, reporting, and long-term sustainability planning.

Culture & People

  • Foster an inclusive, equitable, and collaborative organizational culture that respects and integrates the values of CHOP, Penn, and the Lurie Autism Institute.
  • Lead recruitment, onboarding, and professional development for administrative staff and shared operational resources.
  • Promote transparent communication and collaboration between administrative and scientific stakeholders across institutions.

Education Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree - Required
  • Master's Degree in a healthcare related field - Preferred

Experience Qualifications

  • At least twelve (12) years of clinical research or research administration experience - Required
  • At least ten (10) years of leadership, management or supervisory experience - Required
  • At least three (3) years of grant writing and/or grants management and coordination experience - Required
  • At least three (3) years of financial management experience, including budget preparation and management - Required
  • At least three (3) years of resource management, project management and coordination experience - Required
  • At least twelve (12) years of cost analysis and budgeting or sponsored projects management experience - Preferred
  • At least ten (10) years of leadership, management or supervisory experience in a clinical research or academic environment - Preferred
  • At least five (5) years of financial management experience, including budget preparation and management in a hospital or medical school environment - Preferred
  • At least five (5) years of editing, including manuscript preparation, galleys, proofs, etc. experience - Preferred
  • At least five (5) years of pediatric research experience - Preferred
  • At least fifteen (15) years of clinical, basic, translational research or research administration experience - Preferred
  • At least eight (8) years of leadership, management or supervisory experience in research, research administration, operations, or finance within university, academic medical center, or institute settings; familiarity with CHOP and/or PENN institutional environments is a plus - Preferred
  • At least five (5) years of financial management experience, including budget preparation and management, grants administration, endowment management, and/or donor reporting - Preferred
  • At least three (3) years of resource management, project management and coordination experience - Preferred

​

Skills and Abilities

  • Advanced proficiency with office software (Microsoft Office) including word processing, spreadsheet, and presentation software (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
  • Advanced knowledge of the strategic and execution aspects of clinical and/or translational research
  • Substantial knowledge of the grant submission process
  • Substantial knowledge of the faculty appointment process
  • Substantial knowledge of research, research protocols, etc. (medical school & NIH)
  • Exceptional verbal and written communications skills
  • Exceptional interpersonal skills
  • Excellent customer service skills
  • Excellent time management skills
  • Excellent critical thinking / problem-solving skills
  • Excellent project management skills
  • Excellent organizational skills
  • Excellent analytical skills
  • Excellent leadership skills
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and professionalism
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision
  • Ability to convey complex or technical information in an easy-to-understand manner
  • Ability to collaborate with stakeholders at all levels
  • Ability to be flexible and adaptable to change

​

As a Senior Android Developer, you will serve as a technical anchor for the team, driving application architecture, modern UI paradigms, and taking full technical ownership of major engineering initiatives. You will work across the full software lifecycle—from conceptualization to deployment—ensuring our mission-critical applications remain reliable, performant, highly testable, and scalable.

Architect & Build: Lead the end-to-end technical design, system architecture, and development of complex mobile features for high-reliability environments using modern Android toolsets.
UI Modernization & Standards: Champion modern Android UI development using Jetpack Compose to build responsive, robust, and maintainable user interfaces.
Testing & Quality Leadership: Establish and drive automated testing strategies (unit, UI, and integration testing) to ensure high test coverage, application stability, and prevent regressions.
Technical Leadership & Mentorship: Drive technical excellence across the team by establishing coding standards, conducting thorough code reviews, and mentoring junior and mid-level engineers.
Ownership & Stability: Serve as a self-sufficient, hands-on technical lead accountable for application stability, performance, code quality, and technical debt mitigation.
Project Delivery: Plan, break down, and drive multiple concurrent technical initiatives to delivery, collaborating effectively with product management and platform teams.

  • Modern UI & Jetpack Compose: Proven experience building complex, performant UIs with Jetpack Compose and modern Jetpack libraries.

  • Language Proficiency: Advanced expertise in Kotlin and Java, including deep understanding of asynchronous programming (Coroutines, Flow/RxJava).

  • Debugging & Troubleshooting: Superior root-cause analysis skills for tackling deep-seated OS, native, or multi-threaded bugs.

  • Engineering Ecosystem: Proficiency with modern Android development tools (Android Studio, Gradle), version control (Git), issue tracking (JIRA), CI/CD test integration, and Agile development methodologies.

Preferred / Plus Qualifications:

  • CI/CD Automation: Experience setting up automated build and test pipelines (e.g., Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Fastlane) for continuous integration and delivery.

title: Specialist, Health Plan Provider Engagement
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION Job Summary

Provides support for implementation of health plan provider engagement strategies and activities to drive necessary quality and risk adjustment outcomes. Uses a consultative approach, emphasizing physician engagement and behavior change through actionable data and analytics. Drives value-based care strategies through risk adjustment and quality improvement activities. Focuses on smaller, less advanced Tier 2 and Tier 3 providers, ensuring they have engagement plans to meet annual quality and risk adjustment goals. Drives coaching and collaboration with providers to improve performance through regular meetings and action plans. Addresses practice environment challenges to achieve program goals and improve health outcomes. Tracks engagement activities using standard tools, facilitate data exchanges, and supports training and problem resolution for assigned providers - driving provider participation in Molina's risk adjustment and quality initiatives.

Essential Job Duties

  • Provides support for provider engagement activities including enhancing value-based strategies, and risk adjustment/quality improvement initiatives.
  • Ensures assigned Tier 2 and Tier 3 providers have a provider engagement plan to meet annual quality and risk adjustment performance goals.
  • Drives provider partner coaching and collaboration to improve Medicaid, Medicare and Marketplace quality performance and risk adjustment accuracy through consistent provider meetings, action item development, and execution.
  • Works with provider front-office staff to get the Molina members with the most open gaps on the schedule seen by their assigned provider. Coordinates with Health Plan Community and Member Engagement resources to drive supporting effort on the member side.
  • Addresses challenges/barriers in the practice environment impeding successful attainment of program goals and understands solutions required to improve health outcomes.
  • Drives provider participation in Molina risk adjustment and quality efforts (e.g., supplemental data, electronic medical record (EMR) connection, clinical profiles programs) and use of the Molina provider collaboration portal.
  • Tracks all engagement and training activities using standard Molina provider engagement tools to measure effectiveness both within and across Molina health plans.
  • Serves as provider engagement subject matter expert; works collaboratively with health plan and shared service partners to ensure alignment to business goals.
  • Collaborates with assigned health plan Provider Relations Network team member on operational, provider and member issues.
  • Accountable for use of standard Molina Provider Engagement reports and training materials.
  • Develops, organizes, analyzes, documents, and implements processes and procedures as prescribed by health plan and corporate policies.
  • Communicates comfortably and effectively with internal and external stakeholders, including physician leaders, providers, practice managers, and medical assistants within assigned provider practices.
  • Maintains the highest level of compliance.
  • May require same day out-of-office travel up to 80% of the time, depending upon state/health plan requirements.

Required Qualifications

  • At least 2 years of experience improving population-level HEDIS quality scores and burden of illness documentation accuracy through provider engagement, or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
  • Experience with various managed health care provider compensation methodologies including but not limited to fee-for service (FFS), value-based care (VBC), and capitation.
  • Working knowledge of quality metrics and risk adjustment practices across all business lines.
  • Knowledge and understanding of HEDIS/NCQA and/or CMS STARs quality measures and risk adjustment practices across Medicaid, Medicare, and Marketplace
  • Proficiency with data analysis, manipulation, interpretation, and reporting.
  • Critical-thinking, problem-solving, and analytical skills.
  • Relationship building skills.
  • Attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Ability to implement process improvement initiatives and drive change.
  • Ability to work independently in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
  • Ability to foster and build relationships in a cross-functional highly matrixed organization to obtain buy-in and drive results.
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills.
  • Microsoft Office suite (including Excel), Power BI, and other applicable software programs proficiency, and ability to learn new information systems and software programs.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Nursing, Health Administration or relevant discipline.
  • Solid understanding of health insurance, provider messaging/design, and project management
  • Strong experience using Microsoft products, including Excel (knowledge of pivot tables, VLOOKUP, etc.) and PowerPoint

title: Director, Change Management and Communications, Business Transformation, APEC & GC (Contractual)
description:
JOB SUMMARY

The Director, Change Management and Communications, is a key member of the Business Transformation Office team, reporting directly to the Vice President, Business Transformation Office, APEC + GC (Asia Pacific Excluding China + Greater China). This position is responsible for planning and executing the day-to-day change management and communications activities for the APEC and GC above property and property associates impacted by Marriott’s Digital + Technology Transformation (DTT) program.

The primary focus of the Transformation Office over the next few years will be on designing the user experience and delivering DTT. DTT is a multi-year effort to transform Marriott’s technology and business process ecosystem, enabling Marriott to deliver on our vision to become the world’s favorite travel company. The Transformation Office was established to enable and accelerate DTT through unique approaches to strategic planning, program management, change management, experience and business process design, continent coordination, and deployment.

This role will build upon our existing DTT change management and communications strategies to create and execute the change management and communications plans and related deliverables for on-property and above-property associates throughout the program’s deployment journey, from Design to Stabilize. This role will partner closely with colleagues throughout the entire DTT Program – including (but not limited to) Global Change Management, Communications, Deployment, XD + Business Process Design, Learning, APEC + GC stakeholders and Testing Teams. Success in this role requires strong critical thinking skills, attention to detail, comfort with ambiguity, a proven ability to manage multiple work efforts at the same time, as well as a willingness to be tested on difficult and time-sensitive requests.

Key responsibilities include:

  • DTT Stakeholder Engagement Plan and Execution: Partners with the Vice President and the global Communications team to develop a comprehensive stakeholder engagement plan for APEC and GC and drives the execution of the plan with key stakeholders.
  • DTT Change Management Plan + Execution: Partners with the Vice President and global Change Management to develop the change management plan for impacted associates. Drives engagement of continent subject matter experts during change impact assessments. Partners with global Change Management to execute the plan and related deliverables to drive the required behavior change and shift to desired behavior. Partners closely with the Business Process, Deployment and L+D teams.
  • DTT Recognition Plan: Executes the recognition plan for highlighting quick wins along the journey and ultimately the right behavior adoption. The plan may include gamification, celebratory events, competitions, awards, and/or new supporting tools.
  • DTT Change Management Measurement + Analytics: Directs the day-to-day change readiness and change adoption activities, including scorecards and appropriate forums. Partners closely with the deployment team to develop reports for key MI leaders on readiness pre-cutover and the progress of adoption and highlighting change challenges after cutover (e.g., fatigue, confusion, lack of alignment, etc.)

CANDIDATE PROFILE

Education and Experience

  • 4-year degree from an accredited university; master’s degree strongly preferred
  • 8+ years of relevant professional experience (change management, learning, stakeholder engagement, communications or deployment strongly preferred), demonstrating progressive career growth and pattern of exceptional performance.
  • Experience on-property or above property in the APEC + GC, strongly preferred.
  • Experience with large-scale business transformation, strongly preferred in hospitality
  • Strong personal leadership, organizational, relationship-building, and negotiation skills
  • Outstanding formal and informal presentation skills
  • Self-starter with self-confidence, enthusiasm, and strong customer service orientation
  • Demonstrated ability to deliver results under difficult conditions, particularly when faced with complexity and ambiguity
  • Experience working in or on behalf of (i.e., consulting) a large-scale, global enterprise strongly preferred
  • Excellent English written and oral communication skills; additional Asian languages preferred
  • Experience developing clear, concise, and logically written business communications, as well as delivering recommendations effectively to demanding audiences
  • Ability to gain a clear understanding of an initiative and represent it to various constituencies across the organization
  • Ability to work effectively in a complex, service-intensive, deadline-driven environment

title: NextGen Leader (Part-Time) - Central Dallas
description:
If you are currently on Young Life staff, please do not apply through this external jobs board. To apply for internal job opportunities, log in to Workday and use the Jobs Hub. Applying externally may delay your application and require you to resubmit internally.

Young Life requires all​ employees to sign a Statement of Faith. We recommend you read this statement before applying​ for any position.

Because of Young Life’s exclusive Christian purposes of evangelism and discipleship as set forth in its Articles of Incorporation and in these Bylaws, and to reflect what has always been and will continue to be the position of Young Life, specifically the Christian belief that each and every employee and volunteer of the corporation should minister as a servant of God with the primary responsibility of proclaiming the gospel of Jesus Christ and, as such, is an integral part of the Christian mission and ministry of the corporation,
Young Life shall only employ individuals or enlist volunteer leaders who: (a) profess a belief in Jesus Christ as their personal Savior and Lord; and (b) subscribe to the statements and policies required of all Young Life staff, including the Young Life Statement of Faith. Therefore, employees and volunteers of Young Life, during working and nonworking hours, shall: (i) be ready, willing and able to fulfill such ministry functions as may be required by the organization; (ii) refrain from conduct and statements that detract from the biblical standards taught and supported by Young Life, and (iii) abide by all policies and practices of Young Life including, without limitation, those related to religious belief or ministry activities.

Summary:
Mission / AuthorityThrough both training and direct field ministry experience, learn how to lead and participate in effective Young Life ministry.

Ministry Functions:
Spiritual Development — “Following Jesus” includes prayer and spiritual disciplines, fellowship, growth and health and church relationships.

  • Develop a yearly personal growth plan that fosters a vibrant spiritual life including time for solitude, retreat, reflection, prayer and a sincere commitment to understanding God’s Word.
  • Seek and maintain relationships and disciplines, in the context of active participation in a church community.
  • Actively participate in the spiritual life of the Young Life community.
  • Lead teams and individuals in spiritual development.

Leadership Development — “Equipping leaders, committee and staff” includes key volunteer care, recruiting, team building and training, supervision and vision casting.

  • Meet with your volunteer leaders and area leadership on a regular basis.
  • Learn to recruit and train new leaders to build a leadership team that reflects the community.
  • Model excellence in contact work, club, Campaigners and camping to other leaders.
  • Assist in training leaders, team leaders and committee how to work effectively in teams and develop a yearly ministry strategy.
  • Resource Development — “Fueling the ministry” includes events, major donor care, public relations (branding) and TDS team.
  • Raise financial support as directed and maintain good donor care practices.
  • Communicate ministry updates and progress to personal donor partners.
  • Observe and learn to network and develop strategic relationships with key adults in the community, including: principals, pastors, parents, potential committee members as assigned by the area director.
  • Assist with camp fundraisers.
  • Direct Ministry — “Proclaiming and modeling” includes contact work, club, Campaigners and camp.
  • Actively engage in all three levels of contact work.
  • Lead a team to plan and conduct a new or existing Young Life club and Campaigners/discipleship ministry with excellence.
  • Lead a team to implement a summer and school-season camping strategy for a ministry.
  • Serve on a summer assignment at a Young Life camp each year.
  • Ministry Support — “Taking care of business” includes accounting, administration, communication (internal), data management and strategic plan.
  • Adhere to all Young Life policies and procedures and maintain professionalism concerning office hours, dress, conduct and time management.
  • Manage finances with stewardship, accountability and transparency using the mission-wide applications.
  • Maintain accurate information on kids, leaders and donors for area records.
  • Provide clear, prompt, appropriate and professional communication to everyone involved in ministry.
  • Set yearly strategic ministry plan and initiatives to reach every kid; review them on a regular basis.
  • Perform other duties as assigned and congruent with gifts, experience and area needs.
    ​

Training:
Mission-wide Training

  • None is required.
  • RTD training events such as New Staff Training, Winter Training, Focus Conferences and Young Life University are available on a request basis with approval of the regional director.

Regional Training

  • There is no mission-wide regional-level training curriculum.
  • At the regional director’s prerogative, certain regional training events may be required.

Area Training

  • Actively engage in training provided by area leadership.
  • Individualized training supervised by the area director designed to develop personal spiritual maturity and enhance personal character.
  • Individualized program to learn and gain competency in ministry skills (e.g., The 5 C’s).
  • Become familiar with area strategy and ministry health as assigned by the area director.
  • Introduction to personal fund-raising principles including familiarity with Basic Elements for Part-time staff.

Education:

  • College degree preferred.

Qualifications Required for the Job:

  • Proven relational skills with both kids and adults.
  • Demonstrated verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality.

Job Specific Working Conditions:


The NextGen Leader (NGL) program is a YL National Leadership
pipeline training program intentionally centered around developing
people who are called to make a Kingdom impact with adolescents
from diverse racial and socioeconomic backgrounds.

The Northeast Texas Region is looking to expand their NGL program. If you have gone through the NGL candidate process and have been affirmed, please apply now!
